The Premier League published a redacted 40-page “core decision” from the independent commission, which has taken almost two years to produce after a 42-day hearing that concluded in December 2024.

The league said: “The independent commission found City arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees. The remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano leaving the European Football Clubs board meeting in Copenhagen. Photograph: PA Video/PA

“As part of the scheme, further ‘sham’ arrangements, funded by ADUG, were entered into to enable the club to record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred, as well as a ‘sham’ circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that purchased the club’s players’ image rights, that was funded by ADUG.

“The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900m during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The consequence of this, as the commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators.”

Quick Guide How do I 

ADUG bought City on behalf of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan for £200m in 2008, with the new owners making an immediate impact by paying £32.5m to sign the Brazilian superstar Robinho from Real Madrid. That was the start of a spending spree City struggled to afford from their existing revenues, with the independent commission concluding that the only way to match the owners’ ambitions for the club was for ADUG to “provide very significant funds by way of equity contribution”.

The commission report states that in 2010 City devised a scheme whereby sponsors would pay a “base sum” and ADUG would pay a “tagged sum”, despite the base sum being the only true revenue. The recorded sponsorship fee would be the total of them both.

City’s lawyers claimed that the “tagged sum” was a loan by the Abu Dhabi government on liabilities on sponsorship fees. The commission rejected that argument.

The judgment is a huge victory for the Premier League and Masters. Despite the commission demonstrating that City breached Uefa’s spending limits there appears little prospect of Uefa’s case being revisited because there is a five-year statute of limitations on its disciplinary proceedings. Uefa’s punishment of City in relation to alleged financial fair play breaches was largely overturned in 2020 by the court of arbitration for sport, which found “most of the alleged breaches were either not established or time-barred”.

Masters said: “The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City.”

He said in relation to sanctions: “Now we have the commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the league, our clubs and fans.”

Other Premier League clubs are surprised City have not reached an agreed sanction with the Premier League, given the judgment, but City continue to deny wrongdoing. “Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today,” the club said. “The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.”

Sports.title: Gordon and Kane fire England to Nations League victory against 10-man Czechia
Sports.content:
Anybody can lose to Spain. But when England did so at Wembley on Saturday, it served to turn up the temperature for this trip to Czechia. England have form for finding it difficult at this compact stadium. Remember the European Championship qualifier here in 2019 when they lost 2-1?

It was not easy at first. Thomas Tuchel shuffled his pack, making the surprise decision to start Jude Bellingham among the substitutes. It was all a little angsty and Czechia, for whom this is the dawn of a new era under the Spaniard Santi Denia after their World Cup wipeout, dared to dream of another upset.

Then everything changed. It was a rash challenge in the 23rd minute by Pavel Sulc on Elliot Anderson, late and high, albeit nothing overtly nasty. The referee, Umut Meler, showed the Czechia midfielder a yellow card and on we went. Yet the VAR was not happy and when Meler was called to the pitchside monitor, everybody knew what was coming next.

It was a red card to disfigure the contest but Tuchel was not complaining. His players made the most of the decision to get their Nations League campaign up and running with the standout moment being provided by Tuchel’s headline selection.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was in from the cold at the outset for only his second appearance under Tuchel; the first was as a substitute against Andorra in the summer of last year. It was the Real Madrid player who helped to unlock the stalemate at the beginning of the second half, his whipped cross made to measure for Anthony Gordon.

Harry Kane added the second with his 87th England goal and, after all the focus on England’s defensive vulnerability, there was the bonus for Tuchel of a first clean sheet in seven matches. The team had conceded 13 times in the previous six. It did not start particularly well. By the end, it was a stroll.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane fires home to double England’s lead with his 87th goal for the national team. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

The inclusion of Alexander-Arnold at right-back was the ­wildcard. Any team with him in it feels more nuanced and it meant Tuchel retained only Marc Guéhi from the back four against Spain. Ezri Konsa and Nico O’Reilly had minor injuries. With Trevoh Chalobah in central defence and Lewis Hall at left-back, it was a completely untested unit.

England lacked cohesion at the outset. There were errors from them and it was easy to fret about their lack of care on the ball; the looseness of some of the passing. They were a little open at the back. Czechia were the better team until the sending-off.

England could highlight the moment on 16 minutes when Gordon took a fizzed pass from Myles Lewis-Skelly and crossed low for Morgan Rogers. The man who came in for Bellingham spun and sent a shot against the inside of the far post. But Czechia had flickers. Sulc almost got in after Anderson misjudged a high ball. Lukas Cerv hit a sweet volley past the post. Sulc choose the wrong option when well-placed and was crowded out by Guéhi and Chalobah.

View image in fullscreen Pavel Sulc (left) is shown a red card by Halil Meler for a foul on Elliot Anderson. Photograph: Slávek Růta/Zuma Press/Shutterstock

The red card was devastating for Sulc, and not only because he did not have to jump into the tackle. It was in a non-threatening area of the pitch for Czechia. He overstretched in an effort to win the ball and it did not feel crazily excessive in terms of the force. There was no outrage from the England players around Anderson. At the monitor, though, Meler concluded that it ticked the boxes for an upgrade to red. As always, it looked worse on the slow-motion replays.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Czechia felt their attacking ambition evaporate. England came to dominate the ball. What could they do with it? Not much before the ­interval. Kane took another incisive pass from Lewis-Skelly and extended Matej Kovar in the 45th minute but that was about it.

Tuchel finished the first half in an almighty funk at the fourth official after a decision had gone against Bukayo Saka. The manager reset at the interval, sending on Eberechi Eze for Lewis-Skelly – who was booked on 35 minutes – and going to a 4-1-4-1. Lewis-Skelly had lunged in on Cerv, whose screams could be heard up in the press box. The Czechs wanted a red card to even things up. It was not that bad but Tuchel could not take any chances.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Gordon plants his astute second-half header, from Trent Alexander-Arnold’s cross, into the corner of the net. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

England got the breakthrough almost immediately and it was one for the Alexander-Arnold lovers. When Czechia coughed up the ball cheaply, he chased it down on the right, turned and did what he does. The pinged cross had a low trajectory and it bounced once before sitting up for Gordon, whose headed conversion was marked by precision. It was deserved reward for Gordon, who was quick and urgent; the player most likely to spark England.

England relaxed. They were good thereafter. Hall began to surge up the line. He shot inches wide after getting a pass back from Gordon while he watched Ladislav Krejci turn a low cross from him against the far post. The Kane goal was inevitable and it came when he drilled a loose ball into the far corner after a break into the box by Rogers.

Tuchel got Alex Scott on for his debut and he did well. Ditto Rio ­Ngumoha, who also came off the bench. England might have scored more with Kovar making a particularly fine save to deny Eze. Next up for them is Croatia away on Saturday.

Sports.title: Switzerland’s Rodríguez and Elvedi punish Scotland after Hendry’s early red card
Sports.content:
Switzerland have responded exceptionally well after allegations of capers involving vaccination certificates that threatened to overshadow this international window. Make that six points out of six for Murat Yakin’s stylish team. Switzerland look comfortably capable of breezing out of Group B1 in the Nations League. They have not even played at home yet. Granit who?

Sébastien Pocognoli, conversely, has been left to ponder one step forward and umpteen back. Scotland’s second half in Slovenia at the ­weekend provided hope to the new manager and a supporter base who want to enter a brave new world. Age old, troublesome flaws remain.

Jack Hendry’s red card meant Scotland played almost 80 minutes of this encounter with 10 men. They were, however, outclassed in every department. Scottish patterns of play were not immediately obvious. The upcoming trip to North Macedonia carries importance as Pocognoli seeks to win hearts and minds. This was all pretty grim for anyone of a Scotland persuasion.

“The red card of Jack is all of our red card,” said Pocognoli. “We stay together. We put this moment in our DNA today and hopefully it can be helpful for the future.”

Scottish expectancy heading into a World Cup where they subsequently took tedium to new levels feels a long time ago. They have scored only once in five games. Impotence can only concern Scotland’s Belgian manager, whose bow at Hampden Park was over as a contest long before full-time. A penny for the thoughts of Steve Clarke, Pocognoli’s immediate predecessor and a coach much-maligned in certain quarters. Were Clarke in charge of this ragged display, the public response would have been ferocious.

Judgment of Pocognoli on this occasion requires appropriate context. Switzerland had control of the early exchanges without creating anything until a slick move saw Dan Ndoye sent through on goal from the halfway line. It was quickly apparent ­Hendry did not have the pace to halt his ­opponent. Initially, the referee Nenad Minakovic booked Hendry and awarded a penalty for the clear pull on Ndoye which ­toppled the Swiss forward. Following a video assistant referee check that was unnecessarily lengthy, the official corrected his decision to a free-kick and sending off. Up stepped Ricardo Rodríguez to crack the ball beyond Angus Gunn from 19 yards.

Pocognoli’s immediate response was to withdraw Kieron Bowie, one of two strikers. The introduction of ­Stephen Welsh retained Scotland’s three-man backline. A noticeably subdued Hampden crowd feared a long evening. This is, after all, a Switzerland team that followed up a strong World Cup performance with a comfortable win in North Macedonia on Saturday.

John McGinn appealed in vain for a penalty after claiming he was held at a Scotland corner. The blunt truth is Scotland have needed more from McGinn than the seeking or winning of fouls for some time.

McGinn’s Aston Villa teammate Johan ­Manzambi was unsurprisingly lively; he fired just wide of Gunn’s right-hand post moments after a delicious cross that found no Swiss takers. With half an hour played, the Scots were gasping for air against opponents who looked physically and technically superior. When in possession, far too much of the hosts’ play was sideways or backwards. Gunn denied Ndoye nine minutes before the break.

View image in fullscreen Nico Elvedi celebrates after doubling Switzerland’s lead from close range in the second half. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

The half ended with a yellow card for Pocognoli, who protested a little too vociferously after McGinn was fouled. All the episode did was sum up Scottish frustration. There had been needle in the game but the coherent football had been played by those in red.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Manzambi had irritated the home support by embellishing fouls and entering into a verbal spat with Oli McBurnie. His play, though, was a compelling watch. Manzambi’s movement unnerved Scotland. His willingness to drop deep or wide to get involved in the game emphasised his versatility. His touch and dribbling ability set him apart; all at the age of 20. Scotland’s lack of anything approaching such emerging talent is glaring.

Switzerland’s second came from a more unlikely source. Scotland only partially cleared a corner, with the ball funnelled wide right to Ndoye. The cross was pacy and low, with the central defender Nico Elvedi striding forward to flick home. Two nil was a more appropriate reflection of events to that point.

Pocognoli now made a triple change. McBurnie’s 18th cap had passed without the ending of his international scoring wait. As on Saturday, the alterations were like-for-like in positional nature. ­Pocognoli’s level of tactical flexibility remains open to question. Yakin withdrew ­Manzambi, in what could be classed as a humanitarian act towards Scotland.

Not that Switzerland had stopped dishing out punishment. The ­closing stages resembled an attack ­versus defence training exercise. A third from the Swiss was inevitable as they toyed with the Scots.

Gunn was pitifully weak in attempting to deal with Zeki ­Amdouni’s strike, which flew into the roof of the Scotland net via the goalkeeper. Cue a mass exodus from the stands. Pocognoli has been served a strong, painful reminder of the scale of task he chose to inherit.

Sports.title: Nations League roundup: Lamine Yamal sinks Croatia in Spain’s World Cup homecoming
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup.

Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring within two minutes against England in Saturday’s Wembley win and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic’s side in Andalusia. The teenager’s left-footed finish took his tally of international goals to nine in 36 appearances.

Just before the half-hour mark, the visitors equalised through Dion Beljo’s header as the 6ft 4in attacker headed home from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Two minutes later the hosts restored their lead as Marc Pubill fired home a header from a pinpoint Lamine Yamal cross before provider turned scorer again on 63 minutes, beating Barcelona teammate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at his near post. With fewer than two minutes to play Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams notched up a fourth for Spain with a crisp dribble and finish.

La Roja next play Czechia on Saturday in Group A3.

Lamine Yamal’s contribution strengthened his case for the Ballon d’Or, with voting having closed on Monday and the winner announced on 26 October.

Spain’s captain, Rodri, showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesús Navas, a winner with Spain in 2010.

“We were very excited to bring the cup here,” Lamine Yamal said. “To be able to win the game and bring it home is great.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In Group B1, Slovenia beat North Macedonia 2-0 with goals from Sandi Lovric and Aljosa Matko.

Moldova were held to a 1-1 draw at home to the Faroe Islands and Slovakia beat Kazakhstan 2-1, while Iceland were 3-0 winners in Luxembourg and Estonia drew 1-1 in Bulgaria. Finland and Belarus played to a scoreless draw in Helsinki.

Sports.title: Sham City: verdict on financial breaches is damning and punishment must be severe | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
How bad could it be, really? How serious can a breach of arcane financial regulations be, really? Just how damning can accountancy be? Even after Friday’s revelation that Manchester City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges brought against them by the Premier League, it was perhaps difficult to grasp the scale of what that meant. After the publication of the independent commission’s findings, there can be no doubt: the commission found that Manchester City cheated, that they did so deliberately, and that they have sought to cover that up with a campaign of calculated misinformation.

City continue to maintain their innocence and issued a statement insisting that “the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”. It referred, once again, to “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of all of its positions”, and, again, insisted that “the club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence”.

The chief executive, Ferran Soriano, released a video reiterating many of the same points and vowing that the club would appeal – it has until Friday to do so – and pursue “all other legal avenues” to prove its innocence. He dismissed the Premier League’s charges as “a conspiracy theory” – and pointedly referred to the independent commission as a “Premier League Commission” – claiming that they were based on “a single false accusation” of diverting funds from the owner to the club under the guise of sponsorship payments. This, he said, “could not happen and … did not happen”. The commission’s view, it’s fair to say, is very different.

Any sanction will be addressed separately in a further hearing with the independent commission, but it is impossible to read the verdict without thinking that it will have to be extremely severe. Everton were docked a total of eight points over two accounting windows for an inadvertent breach of profitability and sustainability rules amounting to around £20m, having cooperated with the investigation. Exactly what City’s breach would turn out to be remains to be calculated, but the verdict found that they overstated income by around £855m and understated outgoings by around £66m. And this was not a cock-up but a calculated attempt to circumvent the rules.

View image in fullscreen The Premier League is made up of its 20 constituent clubs. City have cheated each of the other 19. Photograph: Carl Recine/Reuters

The verdict makes for astonishing reading. The reputation and integrity of the Abu Dhabi United Group, the 81% majority owner of City, lies in tatters, shredded in careful, measured legal prose. The appendices, as and when they are made public, might make it even worse. Even if some technicality is found that mitigates the punishment, their standing cannot surely recover. The findings show this is the greatest fraud ever perpetrated on English football. This is not breaching the maximum wage and being caught when most clubs were doing similar, which lay at the heart of the three previous huge top-division financial scandals: Manchester City in 1906, Leeds City in 1919 and Sunderland in 1957. This was deception on a massive scale.

Sponsorship deals are described as “shams” to obscure investment and overstated by £830m over the nine years in question as part of “a plan to disguise shareholder funding … as ‘commercial partner revenue’”. The Fordham Agreement, an arrangement by which an entity bought player image rights, was “little more than a front”. Attempts to claim that the Premier League had misunderstood how the sponsorship deals worked were “an ‘explanation’ that the club concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal and obscure the realities of the disguised funding scheme”.

The level of mendacity identified is extraordinary. In regards to the “sham” sponsorship arrangements there was “intentional conduct” to “disguise the true nature of certain revenues and liabilities/expenses, to give the appearance of minimising the club’s financial dependence on ADUG” and give “a misleading impression in the club’s financial statements that the club’s financial position was better than it in fact was”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Having been charged, City “made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation”. The panel found “evidence given by a number of important factual witnesses called to give evidence on behalf of the club was false in a number of key respects” and “certain of those factual witnesses had given evidence at the hearing that they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest”. On occasions, the panel concluded it “should not accept the opinion of an expert”; the precise reasons why are set out in an appendix but, in context, an inference can be drawn.

The one charge on which City were not found guilty was of breaching “duties of cooperation” with the Premier League in relation to one tranche of accusations. That, clearly, is not the get-out many City fans have hoped for since Friday. The verdict is damning.

The Premier League is made up of its 20 constituent clubs. City have cheated each of the other 19. They have lied consistently and deliberately. The continued denials only enhance the sense that this is a club that has no respect for the regulations.

There must now be a very good argument for expulsion. How can City, at least under the current ownership, ever be trusted again? How can they go on playing even this season, pretending all is well, awaiting appeal and sanction, when they have been found guilty of charges of such magnitude?

When the club has behaved like this, how can its continued existence in the Premier League be tolerated? And when they have cheated as they have been shown to do between 2009-10 and 2017-18, how can their name appear on the Premier League’s roll of honour?

Sports.title: ‘The emperor is naked’: Uefa president Ceferin takes new swipe at Infantino
Sports.content:
The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has attacked his embattled Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino in a scathing takedown of the failed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and other recent scandals, saying “the emperor is naked” and declaring “it is time to say ‘enough’”.

In a pointed address to the European Football Clubs (EFC) general assembly, Ceferin did not mention Infantino by name but made clear his view that Fifa’s leadership must change. He drew on the event’s location, Copenhagen, to make a comparison to Hans Christian Andersen’s The Emperor’s New Clothes in assessing Infantino’s conduct, making clear reference to the peace prize awarded to Donald Trump and last summer’s Folarin Balogun affair along with the FFE scheme.

“An emperor is persuaded that he is wearing magnificent clothes – clothes which, he is told, only the foolish or unfit cannot see,” Ceferin said. “His court goes along with it. Until a child simply says aloud what everyone can see: the emperor is naked. Perhaps the moral of the story is this: convenient words cannot change uncomfortable realities.

“Selling part of football’s future does not become development because you call it development. Putting a fait accompli in front of national associations does not become democratisation because you call it democratisation, however big the cheque is. And secrecy does not become consultation because you call it consultation.”

Ceferin suggested to the ­hundreds of club representatives present that ­Infantino’s behaviour would not be tolerated at one of their organisations. “Imagine one of your senior executives secretly negotiating away control of your club’s crown jewels,” he said. “You didn’t know. Your board didn’t know. Your players and fans didn’t know. And by the time you find out, the deal is almost done. What would your board do?

“Imagine that he creates a peace prize for a political leader, without his own board having any say over its creation or its recipient. Then, that same political leader calls during the biggest competition in the world to complain about a decision on the pitch. The rules say one thing. The phone rings. Then the decision changes.

“How many times would this have to happen at your club before the board says: ‘enough’? I think it is time to say ‘enough’. No office, no title and no amount of power gives anyone the right to sell the future of football.”

The ongoing war of words between football’s biggest governing bodies had already intensified on Tuesday when Fifa accused Uefa of waging a “misinformation campaign” and trying to influence the race for its presidency, urging a US court to reject Uefa’s request to receive documents for use in a planned criminal complaint against Infantino.

Senior figures within Uefa remain adamant that a candidate to oppose Infantino in the Fifa election next March must be found before the 18 November deadline for nominations. The EFC chair, Nasser al-Khelaifi, has been mooted in the past as a future contender but conclusively ruled himself out of the Fifa presidency in the Danish capital.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I have zero interest in Fifa, zero agenda or ambition to be there,” al-Khelaifi said. “I don’t think I’m the right guy for this position. I’m enjoying what I’m doing, having fun. Fifa, not for me.”

Al-Khelaifi has designs on expanding the scope of his own organisation. In his speech to the general assembly he said “now is the time to create World Football Clubs”, explicitly stating that a representative body including those beyond Europe should be formed. “We are more than proud and happy if we can help and contribute outside of Europe for our colleagues from different clubs in the world,” he said later.

Sports.title: Chloe Kelly and Ella Toone dropped by England after not hitting ‘expected’ level
Sports.content:
Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly have been dropped from England’s squad because of their performance levels by Sarina Wiegman, who has given a first call-up to the 20-year-old ­Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter.

Toone and Kelly have played key roles in England’s run of three consecutive major tournament finals but Wiegman made clear on Tuesday, when announcing her selection for the Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff against Greece, that she wants to see more from them for their clubs.

“The main reason is that I think the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch,” Wiegman said. The head coach “still believes in them” but said: “We expect a bit more and we know they can bring more. That was the message.

“There is also competition going on. It’s about talent, it’s about playing minutes and it’s about the ­competition going on. I hope they can step up and show what they can do.

Quick Guide England squad Show Goalkeepers: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea), Khiara Keating (Liverpool), Anna Moorhouse (Manchester City on loan from Orlando Pride) Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Niamh Charles (Manchester City), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Leah Williamson (Arsenal) Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Lucia Kendall (Aston Villa), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Keira Walsh (Chelsea) Forwards: Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Lauren James (Chelsea), Beth Mead (Manchester City), Jess Park (Manchester United), Alessia Russo (Arsenal) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I’m convinced they can do better, I think they are convinced about that, too. I think they took the feedback in a good and in a positive way but it’s hard to take at the same time of course; it’s not a nice message. I hope they respond to it really well. We will support them and of course they get the support at club, too. I hope they come back even better than they were before.”

Neither Toone nor Kelly has scored or provided an assist in the Women’s Super League this season, although Toone did score in ­Manchester United’s 10-1 League Cup victory against the second-tier side ­Sheffield United last week, after she had been left out of their draw at Arsenal. Toone has started three of United’s four WSL games. Kelly has started one of Arsenal’s league matches, their ­Champions League win against Køge and made three WSL substitute appearances.

There was also no place for the Chelsea forward Aggie Beever‑Jones. Wiegman has called up the uncapped 18-year-old midfielder Erica Meg ­Parkinson and the London City Lionesses winger Freya Godfrey, and there is a return after injury for the captain, Leah Williamson.

There had been growing calls for the inclusion of Potter this term after her strong form for Chelsea, ­including her starring role in the 1-0 victory against Arsenal on Sunday. “She’s grown a lot,” Wiegman said.

“Last season we kept a close eye on her because she was getting into the squad and playing really well. But I think she’s started the season so well. Her performances have really impressed us so she really deserves this call-up.

“She’s shown at Chelsea that she can start against any team. The last game I thought she did very well against a top Arsenal [team]. What I’ve seen from her is that she comes out on the pitch and no matter who she plays against, she’s just going to play and she’s comfortable. I hope to see that next week.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Lionesses face Greece in the first leg at the Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion, Crete on Friday 9 ­October before the return at Leicester’s King Power ­Stadium the following ­Tuesday, needing victory to reach the second decisive round of the ­playoffs in December.

England are having to contest the playoffs despite winning five of six matches in their qualifying group, having missed out on top spot to the world champions, Spain, based on the head-to-head record from their meetings in April and June, in repeats of the 2023 World Cup final. England will be heavily fancied to progress to next summer’s finals in Brazil.

That tournament could be ­Wiegman’s last with England because her contract expires after the World Cup. She gave little away when asked about any contract discussions.

“We have regular conversa­tions together, and we talk about the future at moments, but at this point I’m just focusing on Greece. We want to get through and qualify for the World Cup. Of course I talk to Mark [­Bullingham], every two weeks, and we speak about what’s ­happening now, what’s in the future, but there’s nothing new.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa sack manager Natalia Arroyo with club second-bottom of WSL
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have sacked Natalia Arroyo as their women’s manager, with the side winless and second-bottom of the Women’s Super League.

Arroyo was let go on Monday night, after Villa endured a 4-0 defeat at Tottenham on Sunday. It was a second loss in their opening four games of the season, with a 4-1 defeat by Manchester City sandwiched between 1-1 draws with Chelsea and Brighton, with performances largely poor.

Arroyo was appointed in January 2025, signing a three-and-a-half-year contract with the club. The former Barcelona and Espanyol player, who spent time as a journalist before focusing on her coaching career, joined Villa following four impressive years in charge at Real Sociedad where she guided the club to a second-place finish in the 2021-22 season and a Copa de la Reina final in her final campaign.

The 40-year-old replaced Shaun Goater, who took temporary charge following Robert de Pauw’s departure amid allegations over remarks he had made to players. Villa had only two wins from their first 12 WSL games when Arroyo took charge. Five consecutive league defeats followed as the team adapted to the new manager and they won their remaining five games to finish sixth.

Villa finished ninth in Arroyo’s first full campaign, with 20 points from 22 games, but a poor run of form and four successive defeats blighted the end of the season. “Everyone at Aston Villa would like to thank Natalia for her efforts and wish her all the best in her future endeavours,” the club said in a statement.

Villa have confirmed that Brian Sørensen, the women’s technical adviser, will take temporary charge of the team, including for their Subway Players Cup tie against Newcastle on Wednesday. Sørensen joined Villa as technical adviser in March, following his exit from Everton in February after four years with the Merseyside club.

Sports.title: Scotland suffer two damning feats as new manager oversees unwanted 55-year first
Sports.content:
Scotland suffer two damning feats as new manager oversees unwanted 55-year first

Sebastien Pocognoli's start to his Scotland reign has gone from bad to worse after his side suffered a 3-0 defeat to Switzerland.

Following a 0-0 draw away at Slovenia over the weekend, Scotland once again disappointed in the Nations League.



3 Pocognoli has failed to win any of his opening two matches in charge of Scotland Credit: AFP

Pocognoli, who guided Monaco to seventh spot in Ligue 1 last season, was announced as Steve Clarke's successor in August.

Scotland fans were optimistic that the Belgian, who is the country's first foreign manager since Berti Vogts [2002-2004], would build on the feel-good factor following the World Cup.

But Pocognoli has endured a nightmare start, with his first home match at Hampden Park against Switzerland proving to be a horror show.



The hosts were reduced to ten man after Jack Hendry was sent off after just 11 minutes, with Ricardo Rodriguez proceeding to break the deadlock from the resulting free-kick.

And Murat Yakin's men compounded further misery on Scotland in the second half, with Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouni getting on the score sheet.



What unwanted history has Pocognoli overseen?

With no wins from his opening two games, Pocognoli is the first manager to suffer the unwanted feat since George Burley in May 2008.

Pocognoli is still searching for a first Scotland goal, with his side mustering just one attempt against Switzerland on Tuesday night.



It's now four games in a row that Scotland have failed to find the back of the net - the first time this has happened since 1971.

Meanwhile, Scotland have also now failed to keep a clean sheet in their last eight home matches.

That is their longest run since they conceded in ten consecutive home fixtures between October 2001 and September 2003.

3 Scotland will be looking to bounce back with a win in their next Nations League clash against North Macedonia on Saturday Credit: Getty



What has Pocognoli said about Scotland's defeat?

Despite the humbling loss, Pocognoli insists he remains proud of his side for how they fought, despite being a man down for the majority of the game.

The 39-year-old also stressed his pride that Scotland didn't concede five or six goals in their match as he looks ahead to Saturday's clash away at North Macedonia.

He told BBC Scotland: "They [the players] worked with ten men for 80 minutes, maybe more, they showed great character to stick together for that time.

"It's not easy against a good team to be with ten men, it will be more about the reaction because we were so excited to start this first page of the book at home.



"We were ready to deliver the game we wanted from the first minute. We had an unlucky red card, punished with the free-kick, that's the worst scenario.

"We could probably manage the situation better, that's a fact, we create a press where we get the ball back, but from a transition we concede another transition.

3 Scotland are on the cusp of failing to score in five successive games for the first time in their history Credit: Getty

"We could probably defend better, we have to fight with ten men, the guys did the best they could and hopefully we will remember this night differently later on, we have to move on and get a good result in Macedonia.



"We feel sorry for Kieron [Bowie], it's not something we wanted to do [substitute him early] but we had to be smart to keep us alive as long as possible in the game.

"I'm proud because you can collapse in that moment and maybe lose two or three more goals, because they are a team that don't give the ball away cheaply.

"We didn't have a lot of set pieces to maybe have a bit of luck.

"I had a good welcome, it's just frustrating because I said before the game I want to have a good game.

"Hopefully this will be a nice night to remember in the future as part of the process."

Sports.title: Man City board must go and club must be kicked out of Premier League if appeal fails, says former chairman
Sports.content:
Man City board must go and club must be kicked out of Premier League if appeal fails, says former chairman

Ex-Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has called for the removal of the current board in the wake of the club’s guilty verdict.

City were found guilty of all Premier League financial breaches against them by an independent commission on Tuesday.



3 Man City chiefs Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and Ferran Soriano must find a way to overturn the charges levelled at the club in an upcoming appeal Credit: Getty

The club were found to have arranged ‘sham’ contracts with a host of their commercial partners to artificially inflate the club's revenues by around £900m.

City also failed to co-operate in good faith with the Premier League during the investigation.

Club chiefs insist they are innocent and are ‘surprised’ at the panel’s decision. They have until Friday to appeal the decision.



It is understood that the Premier League are eager to conclude the case at the earliest opportunity.

Should they fail in their appeal, then City are facing unprecedented sanctions that could result in a heavy points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.



Bernstein, a boyhood Manchester City fan who acted as chairman from 1998 to 2003, has slammed the club’s dealings over the nine-year period in question and says the position of the current board is now untenable.

Bernstein: Throw the book at Man City board

"I can't think of a penalty strong enough for this, really. I mean, this is absolutely terrible,” Bernstein told talkSPORT Drive.



“I want to raise another question, and that is the position of the board of directors. Because the directors of the club, including the chief executive, who's been there for years and went through this through this period, are responsible for the running of the club in every respect.

“And again, if this was a public company of some sort, I think the directors with something as serious as this, would have to stand down or be suspended pending the outcome of all this... appeal or no appeal.

“I don't think the present management can credibly continue. Now, I doubt if the Abu Dhabi owners would be very happy with that possibility.”

3 Ex-City chairman David Bernstein has called for harsh punishments if the club are unable to overturn the verdict Credit: Getty



Manchester City CEO Ferran Soriano sent a video message to Manchester City staff on Tuesday evening defending the club’s innocence in the face of the damning verdict.

He went on to describe the outcome as a conspiracy theory created by the Premier League.

Bernstein doubled down on his criticism of the board, accusing them of ‘abuse’ while sparing a thought for the club’s supporters.

“What credibility can a board of directors have who've been involved in systematic abuse over a long period?,” Bernstein added.



"You feel sorry for the City fans. I am a City fan of 70 years. I've supported the club. So this is, you know, I find this really doubly hard.

“I don't know the answer,” he continued. “And part of the reason is that until we understand where we are with the appeal process, you know, we don't know whether something's going to be imposed quickly or what.”

3 Ferran Soriano, now engaged in a huge legal battle with the Premier League, insists the club are innocent Credit: Getty

Bernstein then proposed a major sanction for the club in the event that they fail in their upcoming appeal against the charges.



Time to go

“If this got settled now, you could see one source scenario and set of penalties,” he said.

“But if it drags on for a year or two, heaven forbid, that would be the worst thing for everybody. But if it did, then you'd have a different situation. So it's a little difficult to predict. But all I would say is that money is not sufficient now.

“But if this, if these charges stand now and let's say the appeal does not happen or fails, then I'm afraid for the club I love that they've got to come out of the Premier League. This is beyond awful."

Sports.title: Eight England stars handed 8/10 ratings but one player ‘missed an opportunity’ in Czechia win
Sports.content:
Eight England stars handed 8/10 ratings but one player ‘missed an opportunity’ in Czechia win

England returned to winning ways following Saturday's defeat to Spain by easing to a 2-0 win away at ten-man Czechia.

The Three Lions threw away a 2-1 lead to lose 3-2 against the World Cup champions in their Nations League opener.



6 England beat Czechia in Prague thanks to goals from Harry Kane and Anthony Gordon Credit: Getty

But they have now registered their first points of the tournament ahead of this weekend's trip to Croatia, live on talkSPORT.

Following a first half lacking in quality, England finally made their extra man advantage count just two minutes after the break.

The hosts were reduced to ten men in the 25th minute following a horror tackle from Pavel Sulc on Elliot Anderson.



And it was Anthony Gordon who made the breakthrough, with the Barcelona winger getting on the end of Trent Alexander-Arnold's whipped in delivery to head home into the far bottom right corner.

Captain Harry Kane then doubled the visitors' lead in the 69th minute to bring up his 87th goal on the international stage.



The Bayern Munich marksman, who will equal Peter Shilton's record appearances [125] if he plays in England's remaining two matches this break, reacted quickest to a loose ball in the box.

His first-time left-footed strike nestled into the bottom corner as he put his missed penalty against Spain behind him.



What did Adrian Durham say about England?

Reacting to England's performance live on air, legendary talkSPORT broadcaster Adrian Durham said: "There are a lot of things that need to improve for England if they are to win a major tournament, there's no doubt about that.

"But they were taken by surprise with Czechia going down to ten men in the first half, they couldn't really negotiate that properly until after half-time.

"So what I'm going to do, is give Thomas Tuchel a lot of credit for his half-time team talk, a change of [Eberechi] Eze coming on for Myles Lewis-Skelly, a really attacking change, I think it worked.

6 Gordon opened the scoring with a deft header back across goal Credit: Getty



6 Kane put the Three Lions two goals to the good with a clinical finish into the bottom corner Credit: Getty

"All the subs in the second half [Eze, Alex Scott, Jude Bellingham, Rio Ngumoha and Morgan Gibbs-White] really impressed.

"So if you take the second half in isolation, and yes it was against ten men, but those ten men were defending - or trying to defend resolutely - that was their game plan.

"And England beat the ten men, so I don't think we have any complaints about that second half whatsoever."



Here is how Durham rated and slated England's stars from Prague...

Flash Gordon

The ex-Newcastle star is quickly becoming England's man for the big occasions having now scored in three international matches in a row.

Firing in the opener in the World Cup semi-final against Argentina, before grabbing England's equaliser against Spain last time out, Gordon is enjoying his best spell for the Three Lions.

Incredibly, nine of the forward's 11 goal contributions for England have come in 2026 alone.

Gordon has either register a goal or assist in each of his last six matches under Tuchel's tutelage.



A constant threat, Gordon was awarded an 8/10 rating by Durham.

Waxing lyrical over the 25-year-old, he simply stated: "Excellent again."

6 Gordon has scored three goals and supplied four assists in his last six England matches Credit: Getty

Took his chance

Featuring for the first time for England since a 1-0 win over Andorra in June 2025, Alexander-Arnold showed why he is deserving of a spot in the squad.

The Real Madrid right-back was overlooked by Tuchel against Spain, with the German insisting Jarell Quansah was preferred due to his speed and defending.



But the ex-Liverpool man boasts a trait unlike any defender in the squad: his passing.

That was on show throughout the match, producing a moment of magic to set up Gordon with his inch-perfect cross.

While he may have been booed by Real fans over his plays this term, he was one of England's stars players on his return to international action.

Awarded an 8/10 rating, Durham said: "Good runs forward, terrific passing and an assist."



6 Alexander-Arnold could now keep his place for England against Croatia on Saturday Credit: Getty

Needed Mor from him

While Alexander-Arnold took his chance in the line-up, the same can't be said for Chelsea's Morgan Rogers.

The versatile Blues star, who can play as an attacking midfielder or on the left wing, featured in the No.10 slot in place of Jude Bellingham.

But despite hitting the post in the first half, Durham believes that Rogers lacked a cutting edge in the final third.



Given a 6/10 rating, only Lewis-Skelly, who was awarded a 5/10, was rated lower.

Durham said of Rogers: "Missed an opportunity in the No.10 position."

6 Here is how Durham rated England's starters against Czechia

There were also 8/10 ratings for substitutes Eze, debutant Scott, Ngumoha, Bellingham and Gibbs-White.

Mewanhile, manager Thomas Tuchel was handed a 7/10.

Sports.title: Man City CEO fumes at ‘Premier League conspiracy theory’ in first comments after damning charges ruling
Sports.content:
Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano says the guilty verdicts against the club are based on a 'Premier League conspiracy theory.’

It was announced on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges on Tuesday after inflating their financial position by more than £900million as a result of filing inaccurate accounts.



3 Soriano has hit back at the Premier League following Tuesday's blockbuster verdict Credit: Getty

An independent panel found that the club had inflated revenue over a nine-year period as a result of ‘sham’ sponsorship deals, funded by owners Abu Dhabi United Group.

City say they will appeal the decision before Friday’s deadline with the Premier League keen to conclude the case as soon as possible.

The club are now awaiting details of the imposed sanctions.

Despite that, they continue to refute the breaches and maintain their innocence.



City are likely to be the subject of unprecedented punishments with an excessive points deduction, extended transfer bans and even expulsion from the Premier League all possible outcomes.

Soriano addressed the verdict on Tuesday evening in a video sent to employees, describing the decision as a 'conspiracy theory'.



Fighting talk from Man City CEO

"I want to share some information related to the ongoing disciplinary process between Manchester City and the Premier League," Soriano said.

"A document has been made public with an opinion of the Premier League commission that is negative to our interests.



“I want to explain exactly what this is, the next steps and how we are going to continue to defend the club, and finally be vindicated in this process.

"This has gone for so long that it is important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

3 Man City's case was described as 'the most significant in Premier League history' by the Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters Credit: Getty

"Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen.



"This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate that the money did not come from the owner.

“Every other false charge that has been thrown at us - and aggressively marketed and promoted - comes from the simple, central, and completely false accusation.

"Surprisingly for us, and for our lawyers, after nearly two years the Premier League Commission has introduced an opinion that supports the Premier League's conspiracy theory.

“To do so, the opinion had to ignore the extensive evidence provided by the club in order to reach a conclusion that is clearly wrong.



"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and it is unsafe. Remember we have been here before.

3 City chiefs have until Friday to appeal against the charges Credit: AFP

“In 2020 we were also wrongly ruled against for many of the same issues. We appealed to an independent body in CAS (Court of Arbitration for Sport) and we won.

"We will now be relentless in our work. We will focus on the independent appeal process and also all other legal avenues available to us in order to win the case, and we will take all necessary action to protect the club and seek compensation from any party that tries to damage it now, and in the future.”



Man City saga set to rumble on

It could be some time before this case is brought to a close once and for all with City's appeal inevitable.

Sports lawyer Tom Murray said on Drive: "I think we'll be looking at months and years as opposed to days and weeks.

"City have to appeal by the 2nd of October. On my calculations, that means they probably would have received this decision on the 18th.

"Once you're into that appeals process, it's not a rehearing, it's a review process of the original decision. So what that means is there won't be a series of new witnesses that are brought forward and re-cross examined.



"It's very difficult to adduce new evidence. So to introduce new documents, unless you can demonstrate that these weren't available at the time.

"So the appeal process should be shorter than the time is taken from, you know, from the decision in this case and the initial hearing, which was December 2024, this is determined.

"But I think we're looking at a number of months, potentially another year before this is determined."

Sports.title: England legend delivers verdict on Jordan Pickford vs James Trafford No.1 battle
Sports.content:
David Seaman was shocked Thomas Tuchel chose James Trafford ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain, but supports the switch.

The Everton goalkeeper was an unused substitute at Wembley as England were defeated 3-2 by the reigning world champions, with the same drill of Trafford starting and Pickford being benched happening for their second match where they face Czechia, live on talkSPORT.

3 Trafford has only made three appearances for his country

Tuchel explained that he felt Trafford deserved the opportunity following an impressive start to his Premier League campaign starring for new club Leeds United having joined them from Manchester City.

The German revealed that he had planned to give both keepers two games each in the four-match run during the international break.

Tuchel said: "I felt James deserved to get the two matches, that's why we gave him two matches. He started the Premier League season well and is getting minutes as number one at Leeds.

"Jordan [Pickford] did absolutely nothing wrong, but we wanted to use this competition to see how far actually James is."

The 32-year-old has been the undisputed first-choice for the Three Lions since he replaced Joe Hart in 2017, and has never been truly tested - until now.

On talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs, Seaman said: "I was shocked, because we're playing against the world champions, and you know it’s going to be a real test. It’s a bold decision to put Trafford in there.

"I’ve always said that our back-up keepers have not got a lot of caps between them. If anything did happen to Jordan, then we would have been in trouble because his replacement would not have experience.

"Technically, they would be brilliant but experience goes a long way. However, bringing in Trafford at Wembley against Spain was a real test for him and I thought he did brilliant."

A clash of goalkeeping styles

Under Gareth Southgate, Pickford was unchallenged for his spot - a trend that initially looked set to continue under Tuchel after the former Sunderland keeper started every match during the summer tournament and the majority of World Cup qualifiers.

However, Trafford grabbed his chance despite conceding three times in England's last outing.

3 None of Spain's goals were down to bad keeping from Trafford Credit: Getty

Against Spain, the 23-year-old showed his quality by making an impressive save to deny Ferran Torres in the first half, and the goals they conceded were not particularly down to the Leeds goalie.

Notably, this marked the fifth occasion the Three Lions have conceded three or more goals in a fixture since 2022 - with Pickford failing to feature in any of those matches.

Pickford has kept 46 clean sheets in his 91 appearances for England and has been a huge part of the Three Lions' recent success at major tournaments.

Yet Seaman believes healthy competition will elevate standards across the board, adding: "I do think Pickford will be back because he’s been brilliant for England.

"He made some mistakes during the World Cup but you can count all of them on one hand since he started for England. But now it’s about getting a goalkeeper in there to challenge him because we’ve never seen anyone do that.

"It’s good that Trafford is now getting experience in the Premier League playing for Leeds, I was happy with that signing when I saw it. I like the calmness of him and it’s totally different to Jordan.

3 Pickford made little mistakes throughout the international tournament and was praised for his superb performance against Mexico Credit: Getty

"Jordan’s style is quite hectic, he’s very lively even when he doesn’t have the ball. With Trafford, you have someone who’s very calm, he’s a bit like myself. There was Peter Schmeichel and me.

"There's two completely different ways of being a keeper. It’s whatever gets the best out of you. Even at Arsenal, Arteta put David Raya in because he was a lot calmer than Aaron Ramsdale.

"It’s down to whether Tuchel wants that calmness in goal, but it’s two games each and hopefully Trafford can keep a clean sheet."

Who is England's No1?

Trafford's form this season has helped Leeds to fifth in the Premier League table with the former Burnley player keeping two clean sheets in the process.

His lack of experience may be an issue having only played 32 top-flight games before moving to Leeds following his time at Burnley and Manchester City.

Despite it being a frustrating campaign at the Etihad Stadium, Trafford did get experience and started both the FA Cup final and Carabao Cup final for City before his move to Leeds.

While things are heating up for the youngster, it doesn't seem to be slowing down for Pickford either as he has recently won the August Save of the Month award for a record-extending fifth time following his incredible stop against Crystal Palace.

Sports.title: What next for Man City? Club to appeal as damning report has them staring at devastating punishment
Sports.content:
What next for Man City? Club to appeal as damning report has them staring at devastating punishment

Manchester City have until Friday to appeal against the Premier League independent commission's seismic verdict.

The club have been found guilty of all charges against them for breaching Premier League financial rules.

4 talkSPORT understands City intend to launch their appeal before Friday's deadline Credit: AFP

It comes over three-and-a-half years after City were first charged with 115 alleged breaches in February 2023.

Their offences took place between 2009 and 2018, during which time the club won three Premier League titles.

A hearing was subsequently held by an independent commission between September and December 2024.

Almost two years on, City have now been found guilty of every charge brought against them, with the details of the report released.

Damning details of report

The Premier League's statement has uncovered the damning facts behind the case against the eight-time champions.

Amongst them, several notable discrepancies stand out as City await sanctions for their offences.

The club were accused of arranging 'sham contracts' with its commercial partners which consisted of artificially inflated revenue figures understood to be worth £900million.

Their mis-stated accounts also concealed the true state of the club's finances.

Remunerations to players and managers were also withheld, with the club not disclosing how much they had paid out in compensation.

Meanwhile, City are said to have arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, meaning those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees.

4 City have been found guilty of all charges against them for breaching Financial Fair Play rules Credit: AFP

As a result, City were found to have significantly breached both the Premier League and UEFA's spending limits during the period in question.

City have also committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and utmost good faith towards the Premier League.

What's next for City?

City have now been given until Friday, October 2 to respond to the verdict.

talkSPORT understands the club will appeal against the ruling, which will give them the option to either challenge the verdict or challenge the nature of the process used.

However, if they were to choose not to appeal, they could instead look to reduce the severity of any potential punishments.

A sanctions hearing is expected to last for several weeks, but would be blocked from being launched by an immediate appeal from City.

4 Damning details of City's offences between 2009 and 2018 have been revealed by the report Credit: Getty

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has provided clarity on the appeal process, telling Drive: "It's worth noting, before we get into the details that, although a sanction hearing is expected to be the next step, Manchester City have until October 2 to appeal the actual verdict itself.

"We know from City sources they will appeal, we just don't know whether they'll appeal the verdict and then any sanction hearing, or effectively wait until the punishment."

What punishment could City get?

As for the potential punishments City could face, Jacobs pinpointed the sanctions handed out to Chelsea earlier this year.

The Blues were hit with a one-year transfer ban, suspended for two years, and a record £10.75million fine in March for breaching Premier League rules on payments to agents.

However, Jacobs insisted City's refusal to self-report, like Chelsea did, means they're in line for a significantly worse punishment.

Jacobs added: "Non-cooperation tends to lead to a more severe punishment.

4 City now await their sanctions, but a hearing will be delayed if the club launch an appeal this week Credit: Getty

"The other thing is that Chelsea self-declared, it was a new ownership regime, Clearlake-Boehly reported Roman Abramovich immediately in May 2022 when they discovered in due diligence that there were breaches.

"So that's why it's not a perfect comparison, even though the scale of Chelsea charges was also very high.

"The other factor in all of this is that Manchester City and not co-operating are less likely, if they choose to then later down the line try and enter into a settlement with the Premier League to mitigate the severity of the punishments, find that maybe the Premier League aren't prepared to mediate, because ultimately a vast proportion of these charges, nearly a third, are about City circumventing this investigation in the first place."

City's breaches of Premier League and UEFA spending limits also points to previous cases when it comes to potential sanctions.

Both Everton and Nottingham Forest have faced points deductions in recent seasons for breaching the Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules.

The Toffees were deducted eight points during the 2023/24 season for their offences.

Meanwhile, Forest were hit with a four-point penalty during the same campaign.

When will this end?

It could be some time before this case is brought to a close once and for all with City's appeal inevitable.

Sports lawyer Tom Murray said on Drive: "I think we'll be looking at months and years as opposed to days and weeks.

"City have to appeal by the 2nd of October. On my calculations, that means they probably would have received this decision on the 18th.

"Once you're into that appeals process, it's not a rehearing, it's a review process of the original decision. So what that means is there won't be a series of new witnesses that are brought forward and re-cross examined.

"It's very difficult to adduce new evidence. So to introduce new documents, unless you can demonstrate that these weren't available at the time.

"So the appeal process should be shorter than the time is taken from, you know, from the decision in this case and the initial hearing, which was December 2024, this is determined.

"But I think we're looking at a number of months, potentially another year before this is determined."

Sports.title: Bayern chief reveals key reason Florian Wirtz chose Liverpool transfer
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich's Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has revealed why Florian Wirtz chose Liverpool over the German giants.

Rummenigge is part of the board at Bayern and revealed in an interview that Wirtz being promised the No.10 role was why he elected to go to Anfield.



3 Wirtz's blockbuster move to Liverpool has yet to pay off Credit: Getty

He claims that the finances were roughly the same, but former manager Arne Slot told Wirtz he'd be the attacking midfielder in his system.

Wirtz joined the Reds last summer from Bayer Leverkusen in a deal worth up to £116million.

At the time, it was their transfer record, and they were looking to strengthen after winning the Premier League title.



However, the 23-year-old has yet to really catch alight in the top-flight, scoring five goals and providing a further five assists so far.

And in a question about Wirtz potentially returning to Germany and joining Bayern, Rummenigge revealed he was surprised at Wirtz's struggles.



He said: "To be honest, yes. We were given the impression that he chose Liverpool because the manager back then, Arne Slot, had promised him the #10 position, the role he had also played at Leverkusen.

"That was an important factor in his decision to join Liverpool. There were no big differences financially. He made his decision, and we accepted it."



And on potentially going back in for the Liverpool attacker, he said: "First of all, that’s not my job. It’s a matter for the board. And we mustn’t forget that Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry play in that position, and there are other options as well, such as Ismael Saibari.

"There’s no need to spend the kind of money that Wirtz would probably cost to sign a fourth player for that position. That’s why I say: Before making any move, a player needs to think very carefully about it.

"Whether something might still be possible at some point? I don’t know. The question is whether Wirtz is happy at Liverpool.

3 Wirtz isn't alone in his struggles with lots of last season's buys all not hitting the heights they were expected to Credit: Getty



"I can’t judge that. Uli and I were in contact with his father and mother for a while. Then they decided to take a different path, and we respected that."

Klopp's support

Despite a poor start to the Premier League season for Wirtz, his national team manager Jurgen Klopp is fully supporting the former Leverkusen man to come good.

Wirtz has 46 caps and is a key part of the German national team, and Klopp feels he was unlucky to join at an unfortunate time.

He said: “When you look at the overall context, Flo joined Liverpool at a very unfortunate time. It’s about the passing of Diogo Jota. He joined a team with players whose priority was not football at that time, which is very understandable.



"He learned a lot from his first year. Now it is a new season under a new coach, and I think he has started all the games. Physically, he is doing very well.

“The team is starting to find itself again. Attacking players always need a functioning team around them. Everyone who loves football can see what an outstanding player Flo Wirtz is.

3 Germany have had a poor start to life under Klopp, failing to win their first two games Credit: Getty

"We can’t do more than build him up in our team with enough training and playing time—bit by bit giving him certainty and a good feeling before sending him back to Liverpool. I wish him all the best."



Carragher isn't so sure

On the flip side to Klopp is Jamie Carragher.

The Reds legend has become one of the best pundits around, and he feels that Wirtz isn't going to get better.

Speaking after Liverpool's 1-0 win over Bournemouth to Sky Sports, Carragher said: "That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.



"But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.

"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting."

Sports.title: Why JJ Gabriel could stay at Manchester United amid transfer interest from European giants
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel could remain at Manchester United despite him wanting to leave because of transfer regulations over players of his age.

That's according to European football journalist Kevin Hatchard, who has warned the 15-year-old about the importance of him making the right decision for the next stage of his career.



3 United were shocked by the news of Gabriel wanting to leave, but an exit is by no means fully certain Credit: Getty

As talkSPORT reported earlier in the month, teenage star Gabriel has asked to leave United in what was a surprise decision for the Premier League club.

The forward scored 26 goals for the club's youth sides last season and bagged a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League just days before news of him wanting to depart Old Trafford broke.

Gabriel travelled to Spain for talks regarding a potential move, with Barcelona and Real Madrid understood to be viable options for him.



However, Barcelona sporting director Deco dismissed their interest in an interview with talkSPORT last week, which could be a huge boost to United's hopes of keeping him.

European giants must wait for Gabriel

Drive host Andy Goldstein claimed the European giant's stance on Gabriel sounded like 'a big fat no', to which Hatchard agreed before explaining the difficulties that clubs would face with a deal.



"What I would say is that the player is still 15 and he wouldn't be able to make a move until he was 16. I don't think he can have a proper agent until he's 16 either.

"Realistically, obviously conversations do happen. We have to take Deco at his word but it doesn't mean that Barcelona, when he turns 16, wouldn't be part of that race and wouldn't be interested.



"Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern (Munich), PSG (Paris Saint-Germain), any of these clubs, it would be remiss of them not to at least be aware of him and aware of a possible market opportunity.

"If you look at Bayern, for example, they brought Jamal Musiala to the club from Chelsea at 16, and look what he's gone on to do for them.

"These clubs are very aware of this kind of situation but, at this stage, they can't be seen to be making a move for a player that young."

3 Gabriel turns 16 next month so, as of now, he cannot complete a move elsewhere Credit: Getty



Drive co-host and former England striker Darren Bent then asked: "Although Bayern Munich's a great club, one of the biggest in the world, it does sound like he's got his heart set on Barca or Real Madrid in LaLiga.

"Do you think there could be a situation where he ends up going somewhere that his heart doesn't necessarily want, or go back to Manchester United?"

Hatchard insisted: "Well, him and his family have got to make that decision, haven't they? I don't know a huge amount about him and his situation, but any player of that age has to really think of so many things.

"Can I deal with the move, in general, to a different country? Can I deal with the pressure of being involved with that particular club?



"Do I back myself to make it through to the first team? If that isn't going to happen, can I get loan moves and get miles on the clock?

"Musiala didn't just appear, it took him a little while. They put him through what they call the campus system there at Bayern. I think any player of his kind of age has got to think about opportunity.

3 Gabriel is yet to make a senior appearance for United, but is one of the most highly-regarded talents in the country Credit: Getty

"How am I going to develop? How am I going to play for a first team? What's going to be best for me as a person, my family?



"So many things go into it and if you get it wrong, it can be really tough because you get forgotten quickly in this game, so it's really, really important to get that right."

Sports.title: Star players leaving, abuse from rivals and 'am I going to be put out on the street?': This is what happens when an English sporting super power is found guilty - and what Man City could learn from Saracens' relegation as they battle the same lawyer
Sports.content:
Seven years ago, the barrister fighting the Premier League’s corner against Manchester City took down another of English sport's super powers.

Following bombshell revelations by Daily Mail Sport in 2019, Saracens – then this country's most dominant rugby club and the reigning English and European champions – were found guilty of breaking the Premiership salary cap, in a case led successfully by Adam Lewis KC. Now, Lewis has his sights set on City.

Saracens were mocked, fined £5.3million and relegated. They were hit with their first 35-point punishment in November 2019, after co-investments with star players such as Maro Itoje, Owen Farrell and Billy Vunipola were not disclosed as part of the club’s spending.

Four days later, they had to go and play at Gloucester, whose supporters provided a glimpse of what life could be like for City after the club were found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.

In their first game back after this international break, Enzo Maresca's team enter the cauldron of Anfield – which was vitriolic enough towards visiting City sides even before they were found guilty.

At Kingsholm in 2019, Gloucester fans waved fake £50 notes and shouted ‘cheats’ at the Saracens players.

‘No one really liked Saracens before, so that went to an extreme,’ former Sarries forward Jackson Wray tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Everything came out in the news during the November international break and a few days later we got off the bus at Kingsholm.

In 2019, Saracens – then this country's most dominant rugby club and the reigning English and European champions – were found guilty of breaking the Premiership salary cap

Fans of rival clubs such as Gloucester took delight in sticking it to Saracens once their guilt had been uncovered

Jackson Wray (centre) stayed at the club that he joined as a 14-year-old when they went down to the Championship

'I remember it very clearly. People were throwing Monopoly money up in the air so it fell around us. People stuck celery to caps and threw them at us.

'We got abused on every away game but what can you do? Turn around and say, “I don’t fancy it today” or fight for the club that a lot of us had been at since we were 14 years old? We won the game in the end, which was very satisfying.’

The league's investigation had been taking place throughout the summer of 2019 – with the bombshell findings revealed to the squad when they reconvened after that year’s World Cup in Japan. There was a sense of shock, with the initial points deduction immediately leaving the club in a battle to avoid relegation.

‘When it’s fresh and it’s new, you’re all of a sudden going, “What’s fact and what isn’t fact?”' says Wray. 'Anyone can have an opinion. With City, you see opinions everywhere. A lot of it is based on emotion.

‘Luckily for us, we were all in the training ground that day and speaking to the CEO directly. They won’t be knowing what’s going on and it’s a very strange situation. They’re saying, “We’re sorting it out, you may hear bits”. The Man City players are all on international break, so no one’s together. They’re hearing all sorts in the news and all sorts on X. They’re probably waiting to get back and find out what’s going on.

‘All we could do was keep playing. We weren’t sitting there wiping each other’s eyes. It’s an attritional, dangerous sport so you can’t be too preoccupied. We wanted to go out there and win and shut up the fans who were booing us when we got off the bus. We still wanted to win every weekend, win the league, fight off relegation, save people’s opinions of you.'

Then, with the club unable to meet the salary cap for the 2019-20 season, a further 70-point deduction came, to ensure once and for all that Saracens finished bottom of the table and dropped into the Championship.

‘The picture changed a bit through the season,' says Wray. 'We had our initial fine and points deduction and then our focus turned to, “Right, can we get enough points to stay up?”. Then another 70 points got deducted from us, so we weren’t staying up, and then you’re playing for different reasons…’

Doubling down on the points deduction placed the club’s future into graver threat. Suddenly livelihoods were at risk and world-class players were left with the predicament of how to navigate a year in the second division. In its moment of crisis, the club reappointed its former CEO Ed Griffiths to come up with a survival plan.

Maro Itoje was one of the Saracens stars who stayed for the season in the second tier

It wasn't all plain sailing for Saracens, who lost to Cornish Pirates in week one and finished second in the Championship table before beating Ealing Trailfinders in the promotion play-off

Manchester City might find it harder to retain the likes of Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias in their primes if they are relegated

‘I left in 2015 and came back for 26 days to try and sort it out,’ Griffiths tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘The big question was whether we appealed or not. At the time, we took a decision not to appeal. We accepted the sentence and got all the bad stuff out, meaning we could start the recovery from the Championship.

‘At the moment, City are deciding whether they accept whatever punishment comes their way or they appeal. You suspect they will appeal.

‘Fundamentally, people all asked the same question: “Am I going to get paid? Is my contract still going to be good?” We were able to assure people that they were and calm those nerves. It was unwanted and difficult but once people knew they weren’t going to be put on the street, then they were relatively calm. Everyone was paid what they were owed.
