World.title: Satirist launches site naming Cornell students accused in gang-rape lawsuit
World.content:
Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

Toby Morton, who wrote several episodes of the animated comedy series "South Park," launched a website seeking accountability in connection with an alleged 2024 sexual assault case involving seven fraternity members at Cornell University in the US. The site names seven men accused of sexually assaulting a 20-year-old woman who was allegedly unconscious after being given drugs and alcohol at a Cornell fraternity house, and collects personal data and photos of the members involved.

"I've received messages reminding me I'm not a journalist, I'm 'just a satirist,'" Morton wrote in a September 27 Instagram post regarding the creation of his website TheCornell7.org. "This is true, but it makes me more dangerous," he added, saying he has "nobody to tell me I've gone too far."

The case has recently drawn a surge in public attention after the accuser, identified as Jane Doe to protect her identity, filed a lawsuit in mid-September. Her complaint alleges that she was brutally sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity while unconscious after being pressured to take ketamine, smoke marijuana and drink alcohol at the fraternity house on Cornell's campus in Ithaca, New York. The university, she said in the lawsuit, failed to protect her. Cornell conducted an internal investigation after the incident, but no one was charged.

The reopening of the case has caused renewed attention on social media Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance

Since the lawsuit was filed on September 16, the case has generated widespread commentary on social media. Some have criticized Cornell and the district attorney's office, while others have questioned the allegations.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who handled the original case, said his office has reopened it and plans to present evidence to a grand jury amid public questions about why no criminal charges were initially filed.

Van Houten said in a statement that his office is considering bringing criminal charges related to the incident, though the allegations in the civil complaint are "dramatically different" from the woman's statement to police two years ago — in her statement to authorities, she did not allege she was drugged without her knowledge or that she did not consent to engage in sexual acts.

Justice sought

Cornell's Chi Phi chapter was barred from campus after the alleged incident in 2024. The woman who accused the men of sexual assault dropped out of Cornell University, according to her attorney.

One of the most chilling allegations of the lawsuit is that a message was sent to a Chi Phi Snapchat group at about 1:42 a.m., inviting members to the room to abuse Doe, who was heavily under the influence of drugs and alcohol. The lawsuit alleges that more men then entered the room and that the assault continued for several hours until Doe lost consciousness.

"There were so many people that could have prevented it and they didn't. I've never seen anything like it," an attorney for Jane Doe, Thomas Giuffra, told CBS.

Giuffra pointed out that two of the seven accused fraternity members were expelled, while the others received lesser disciplinary measures.

"Not one of these guys was arrested," Giuffra told the network.

Actress Florence Pugh described the allegations as 'horrific' on social media Image: Cover Images/picture alliance

Politicians and actors speak out

Many people, from US politicians to Hollywood actors, have spoken out about the case in recent days. US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York Democrat, condemned what she described as a "culture of rape" protected by elite institutions.

"When I read what happened at Cornell, those men posted in a group chat. That means it was normal to them. That means it was acceptable to them. This is a culture, and what we must do is understand that we cannot protect those spaces anymore," she said Sunday at a forum near Cornell's campus.

British actress Florence Pugh described the allegations as "horrific" on social media and expressed her support for the student involved.

Pugh, who is currently on a promotional tour for her upcoming Netflix series "East of Eden," wrote a lengthy statement on Instagram, saying that "Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world. You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won't be harmed in return."

"Those who protect and impose light sentences on men who rape and destroy lives should be punished and closely scrutinized. Why are you protecting someone so fiercely?" she wrote.

American actor Josh Gad, best known as the voice of Olaf in Disney's"Frozen" films, also commented on the Cornell case, criticizing what he described as insufficient disciplinary consequences for the students accused of sexual assault. In an Instagram post, Gad said sexual violence should not be treated as a mistake or addressed with limited disciplinary action by a university.

He argued that the alleged conduct had "destroyed a life" and called for greater accountability.



Edited by Joshua Lang.

World.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
World.content:
The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

At the end of October 2026, the first ever Olympic event on African soil will take place as the Youth Olympics comes to Senegal.

Around 2,700 young athletes are expected to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports, with many qualifying through the African Youth Games last year.

"We were entrusted with hosting this event and that is why from Johannesburg to Nairobi, from Dakar to Djbouti, it is all of young Africa that is watching you and watching you with pride," Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye said at the arrival of the flame.

The moment marks yet another step forward for global sport in Africa. In 2025, the first major road cycling event took place on the continent, and in September this year it was announced the first-ever World Athletics Championships would be held in Kenya in 2029. There are also on-going negotiations about Formula 1 returning. It appears that 16 years on since the 2010 World Cup in South Africa, global sport is finally returning to different parts of Africa.

"This is a victory for Africa. It opens the door for Africa to host major events," Malick Diouf, head of a marketing agency and founder of the Dakar Sport Summit, told DW.

"Africa is in the process of opening up to the world, hosting major events and everything. And all of Africa must celebrate this kind of victory."

Malick Diouf believes Africa as an Olympic host is the logical next step Image: DW

With more major events in Africa, the question around an Olympic Games being on the continent looms.

Sports scientist Kamilla Swart has said awarding Africa a Games would make the world "take Africa more seriously." Diouf believes it's the logical next step.

"The Youth Olympic Games, it's a major test for Africa. And I think this is where we need to succeed in organizing these Games and also in sending a message," Diouf said.

"We, Africa, are ready to host the Summer Olympics, and I think that would be the logical next step after the Dakar Olympics. We have Olympic champions; we have record holders; we have Olympians, so we deserve to host the Olympic Games."

Senegal an attractive option for many reasons

The move to re-use and refurbish existing facilities rather than build whole new ones is likely why Senegal's bid was so tempting for the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

The fear of the white elephant facility appears to have been considered here. The Iba Mar Diop Stadium, the track and field stadium, is expected to be used for athlete training ahead of the 2028 Olympics.

"It’s by using these facilities, by participating in and hosting international events, and by consistently maintaining them to the required standards, that we’ll be able to keep these stadiums up to the standards they currently meet," Diouf said.

There's also the social and economical impacts of the Youth Olympics. Diouf believes the impact is beyond just infrastructure, but into roads, the development of the hospitality, security and broadcasting sectors and the young athletes themselves.

"There's life after the Games. Now we need to figure out how to use the resources we have, we need to develop and capitalize on what we have showcased during the Games," said Diouf.

Senegal gears up for Youth Olympic Games To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Future of Youth Olympics in doubt

The significance of these Games stretch beyond even the history they are making in Africa. In May of this year, IOC President Kirsty Coventry put the brakes on the future of the Youth Olympics, leaving real doubts as to whether there will be any more after the 2028 winter edition.

"We need to pause and have a real reflection on why we're doing the Youth Olympic Games and we realized that across the Movement it's very disjointed. There's not a true North Star of why we're doing the Youth Olympic Games," Coventry told reporters.

"So the EB (IOC Executive Board) decided to pause the 2030 process right now so there will not be an election in June, and rather we need to take a step back and develop a youth strategy."

The Youth Olympics in Dakar might well be the last summer edition of the youth games, adding even more importance to the first ones in Africa Image: Nicolas Remene/Le Pictorium/IMAGO

A lot has changed since the Youth Olympic Games were launched in 2010. Initially it was seen as a way to engage a younger audience (athletes were limited by age to between 15 and 18) by trialing new sports as well as testing host country's on a smaller stage. However, with the age of athletes decreasing and the challenges of engaging a younger audience in the modern sports entertainment landscape even more challenging, it appears clear the IOC are reconsidering their options when it comes to investment.

"My only wish is that Dakar be memorable and that people reconsider their decision not to host the Games in 2030," Diouf said.

"I don’t want these to be the last Youth Olympic Games, but if these are to be the last Youth Olympic Games, we need to go out with a bang. Dakar needs to show the world what Senegal is all about, what Africa is all about."

From October 31 to November 13 this year, Senegal will have the chance to do just that.

Edited by: Chuck Penfold

World.title: Los decretos de vivienda llegan al Congreso sin estar amarrados y Podemos y Junts avisan: “Mirad el marcador”
World.content:
El Gobierno lleva negociando semanas con sus socios de investidura los decretos sobre la situación crítica de la vivienda que se han aprobado este martes en el Consejo de Ministros y que se quieren someter a convalidación con urgencia este viernes en el Congreso por varias razones, desde sociales a políticas. Pero ninguno de los dos decretos “están amarrados ni tienen segura su aprobación”, según admiten fuentes del Ejecutivo. “Hemos hecho una apuesta”, razonan esas fuentes gubernamentales, que auguran que será difícil de explicar un rechazo de la mayoría de investidura al primer texto con las medidas que protegen frente a los desahucios hasta 2030 y ayudas a los propietarios. La derrota del segundo decreto sobre la prórroga automática de los alquileres la dan por descontada algunas fuentes tanto del Gobierno como de los socios. Desde Junts solo han anticipado al Gobierno un consejo para el viernes: “Mirad al marcador de las votaciones”. Podemos tampoco aclara su posición por ahora de máximos.

El Congreso volverá a vivir el viernes otra jornada frenética llena de incertidumbres, cada vez más frecuentes en esta taquicárdica legislatura. En el Gobierno contaban con ese tipo de escenarios parlamentarios para la recta final ya casi en campaña, pero ese terreno se ha precipitado con el desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal y la conexión emocional que ha calado en la calle y las movilizaciones convocadas por el Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos. La mayoría de investidura lleva meses bloqueada. Hace un año ya que Junts rompió sus peculiares relaciones y transacciones con el Ejecutivo y no anticipa nunca su voto en casi ningún proyecto. Podemos dejó de ser previsible también hace tiempo y expresa las críticas más duras a cualquier iniciativa de La Moncloa.

“No tenemos nada amarrado. Ni Junts ni Podemos nos han dicho nada, hace tiempo que no podemos contar con saber antes de una votación su voto y hemos decidido hacer una apuesta porque creemos que en el primer decreto no podrán justificar de ninguna manera su voto en contra”, exponen sus planes con sinceridad interlocutores frecuentes del Gobierno con esas formaciones. Lo dicen con un tono de resignación asumida, pero inevitable: “No hay otra opción, sabíamos que este momento iba a llegar al final de la legislatura”. Y relatan: “Cuando le preguntamos a Junts nos dicen: Mirad al marcador de las votaciones”. Con Podemos, la relación no es ni mucho más fácil ni más programable.

La secretaria general y portavoz de Podemos en el Congreso, Ione Belarra, suele acusar al Ejecutivo de Pedro Sánchez —del que formó parte— de haberse entregado en todo a la derecha. Este martes, en el Congreso, tampoco quiso adelantar cuál será el voto de los cuatro diputados de Podemos, tan indispensables como todos los demás que refrendaron hace tres años la investidura de Sánchez. Aquella ecuación se ha repetido muy poco en los últimos meses y aquellos grupos se han atomizado aún más.

En la votación del viernes sobre la que Junts aconseja al Gobierno que esté pendiente del marcador de escaños a favor no se puede escapar ninguno. PP, Vox y UPN, más el integrante ahora del Grupo Mixto Javier Ortega Smith cuentan de partida con 171 noes seguros. El PP no ha llegado ni a plantearse en serio la abstención porque rechaza frontalmente el modelo de regulación o el intervencionismo sobre el mercado de la vivienda del Gobierno y porque se queja, además, de que nadie les ha llamado para hablar. El Ministerio de Vivienda tampoco ha contactado con Vox porque da esos apoyos por imposibles.

Varios componentes del Gobierno, desde la mesa de la rueda de prensa tras el Consejo de Ministros y más tarde Félix Bolaños, Ángel Víctor Torres o Arcadi España en la sesión de control en el Senado, aprovecharon sus plataformas para interpelar al PP a que no se enmiende a sí mismo y rechace el viernes propuestas en favor de los propietarios o los inquilinos que han introducido en los últimos meses en proyectos ya registrados en el Parlamento. Bolaños llegó tan lejos como para emplazar a los populares a prestarse a “quitar algo de poder a los que tienen demasiado y dar algo a los que no tienen nada y no dejar en la calle a Maricarmen”. La pregunta de la senadora del PP había cuestionado al ministro de Justicia sobre presuntas narco injerencias contra la labor de la juez de Extremadura que investigó el caso del hermano del presidente Sánchez. Al presidente del Senado, Pedro Rollán, le desagradó tanto la digresión de Bolaños que le llamó al orden para que se atuviera a la cuestión. Bolaños no le hizo caso por su parte, como tampoco otros senadores y ministros en otras intervenciones.

La añorada mayoría de investidura al completo alcanzaría 179 votos a favor, pero esa meta ya no está nada clara y por ahora solo están más o menos comprometidos para el viernes 168 síes, si se incluyen en esa partida los cinco parlamentarios del PNV, 121 del PSOE, 26 de Sumar, siete de ERC, seis de EH Bildu, uno del BNG, otro de Águeda Micó (Més-Compromís) y el posible de Coalición Canaria, que todavía no lo ha materializado porque aunque reclamó durante toda la tarde del martes los decretos a sus interlocutores no los había conseguido siquiera recibir.

Junts sigue sin decantarse. Fuentes de su cúpula insistieron ya en la tarde del martes, tras conocerse la aprobación de los decretos en el Consejo de Ministros, en el mismo recelo que habían expresado por la mañana: “A estas alturas podemos confirmar que la situación es esta: hasta que no tengamos los textos definitivos no haremos ninguna valoración, ya que nos consta que, aunque han explicado que tienen un acuerdo, en este momento todavía no tienen ningún texto cerrado”. Siete votos en el aire. En el Ejecutivo cuentan con ellos para el primer decreto.

En Podemos, por la mañana, Belarra pidió que los decretos no se troceasen y se apuntó a las demandas máximas del Sindicato de Inquilinas, con expropiaciones incluidas a los pisos de los fondos buitres. Por la tarde remachó que sus cuatro votos serán “una herramienta en manos de toda la gente que se está movilizando en la puerta del Sol” e insistió en que el Gobierno había disgregado en dos los decretos en una estrategia de “divide y vencerás que no va a funcionar porque la gente ve la trampa”. Exigió al PSOE una rectificación y un decreto único, algo que no ocurrirá. El Gobierno espera que Podemos no se desmarque y acabe entrando a jugar en ambas votaciones, pero sin ninguna seguridad. Si Podemos votase a favor la mayoría progresista podría sumar 172 síes y Junts hasta podría abstenerse.

La desafección de algunos socios de izquierdas con el fondo y las maneras con que el Gobierno ha tratado esta crisis desatada con el caso del desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal la resumieron muy bien el portavoz de ERC y el del BNG. Gabriel Rufián lamentó que no era “suficiente” lo acordado pero prefirió subrayar que en estos casos lo “útil” es ser “pragmático con victorias parciales antes que la épica de las derrotas totales”. El gallego Néstor Rego suspendió al Gobierno por fragmentar los decretos pero asumió el voto a favor: “Si hay que escoger entre un parche y dejar la gente desprotegida, el BNG votará a favor de proteger la ciudadanía”.

World.title: La energía que viene a transformar Europa
World.content:
Moeve trabaja en la construcción del Valle Andaluz del Hidrógeno Verde, un proyecto con el que España se pondrá a la cabeza de Europa en la producción de esta fuente de energía renovable.

Las moléculas verdes, como el hidrógeno renovable o los biocombustibles de segunda generación, juegan un papel fundamental para ganar independencia energética y competitividad industrial. Moeve prepara un plan para convertir a España en uno de los principales productores del continente.

La industria europea se enfrenta al reto del siglo: la búsqueda de fuentes renovables, alternativas a los combustibles fósiles, mientras trata de mantenerla seguridad del suministro y conseguir una mayor independencia energética sin perder competitividad.

La electrificación es una de las soluciones más extendidas para descarbonizar el modelo de producción de energía, pero no es suficiente. Es ahí donde entran en juego las denominadas moléculas verdes, como el hidrógeno renovable o los biocombustibles de segunda generación. España, de la mano de empresas como Moeve, se prepara para ser uno de los mayores referentes del continente en su producción y distribución.

Los combustibles de segunda generación y el hidrógeno verde son una alternativa para el transporte por aviación, uno de los sectores más difíciles de descarbonizar. MOEVE

Los biocombustibles se elaboran a partir de residuos orgánicos, como los aceites usados de cocina y desechos agrícolas, ganaderos o forestales, evitando el uso de materias primas que compitan con la alimentación. Su uso puede reducir hasta en un 90% las emisiones netas de dióxido de carbono(CO2)en todo su ciclo de vida, comparado con los combustibles convencionales. El hidrógeno verde, por su parte, se produce a través de la electrólisis, un proceso químico que separa las moléculas de agua en hidrógeno y oxígeno usando electricidad procedente de fuentes renovables como la solar o la eólica. “Los biocombustibles de segunda generación ofrecen un perfil de sostenibilidad significativamente superior a los convencionales”, explica Carlos Olivares, director del Negocio de Biocombustibles y Comercialización de Moeve. Olivares detalla su ventaja principal: pueden utilizarse en motores, infraestructuras logísticas y sistemas de almacenamiento y distribución ya existentes, “evitando inversiones masivas en nuevas redes o tecnología”.

Estas fuentes de energía tienen un papel relevante para descarbonizar los sectores más difíciles de electrificar; como el transporte aéreo, el marítimo y el pesado por carretera o las industrias que requieren grandes cantidades de energía térmica. En estos segmentos, detalla Olivares, las alternativas eléctricas “no ofrecen actualmente la autonomía o competitividad necesarias para operar a gran escala”.

Los biocombustibles de segunda generación ofrecen un perfil de sostenibilidad significativamente superior a los convencionales Carlos Olivares, director del Negocio de Biocombustibles y Comercialización de Moeve

La aviación es el ejemplo más claro de estas ventajas, ya que los combustibles sostenibles (SAF, por sus siglas en inglés) son “la única alternativa disponible a gran escala para reducir significativamente las emisiones de los vuelos demedia y larga distancia”.

Los biocombustibles de segunda generación son, además, una fórmula indispensable para aumentar la independencia energética. Según el informe ¿Por qué Europa necesita las moléculas verdes?, elaborado por Moeve en colaboración con la consultora PwC, el desarrollo de este tipo de compuestos podría reducir la dependencia del exterior que tiene la Unión Europea a la mitad, desde el 57% hasta el 28% para 2040. Algo especialmente relevante en países como España, que utiliza casi un 70% de energía importada.

Según el informe, el papel creciente de las moléculas verdes las llevaría a sustituir hasta un 50% la demanda actual de combustibles fósiles en Europa en 2050, representar un tercio del mix energético europeo y reducir las emisiones de CO 2 en un 22%.

La oportunidad de España

España, precisamente, puede aportar mucho a la configuración del nuevo mapa energético europeo. “Tenemos una oportunidad real de liderar la descarbonización”, indica Alfredo López Carretero, director del departamento de Química de Moeve. El directivo enumera los argumentos para ello: la elevada presencia de energías renovables, el potencial en biomasa, el crecimiento en biometano y una posición “muy competitiva” para desarrollar moléculas verdes como el hidrógeno, el amoníaco o el metanol renovables.

En España tenemos una oportunidad real de liderar la descarbonización Alfredo López Carretero, director de Sostenibilidad del departamento de Química de Moeve

El hidrógeno renovable, en concreto, es una “pieza clave de la transición energética”, según López Carretero. “Si somos capaces de producirlo de manera competitiva, podemos atraer y mantener nuestra actividad industrial”, afirma el directivo. Sus usos son diversos: desde la descarbonización de la industria, como la química o la de fertilizantes, hasta la producción de combustibles sintéticos para la descarbonización del transporte aéreo, marítimo o pesado por carretera. “En Moeve creemos que España puede transformar su ventaja renovable en una ventaja industrial. El hidrógeno renovable puede marcar una gran diferencia frente a competidores internacionales”.

Para aprovechar las ventajas que ofrece España, Moeve desarrolla el Valle Andaluz del Hidrógeno verde, uno de los mayores proyectos de hidrógeno renovable de Europa, en las localidades de Palos de la Frontera (Huelva) y San Roque (Cádiz). María Molina, directora de la iniciativa, resume en una frase su importancia: “No se trata únicamente de producir una nueva fuente de energía, sino de desarrollar una cadena de valor capaz de atraer inversiones, generar empleo cualificado y reforzar la competitividad de la industria nacional”.

Andalucía, punto estratégico en el mapa del hidrógeno verde El impulso de las moléculas verdes El hidrógeno renovable permitirá avanzar en la descarbonización de los procesos industriales y favorecer el desarrollo de combustibles renovables. Con la primera fase del Valle Andaluz del Hidrógeno Verde, Moeve prevé producir unas 45.000 toneladas anuales y evitar en torno a 250.000 toneladas de CO₂ cuando alcance su pleno rendimiento Una nueva generación de combustibles Los biocombustibles de segunda generación se elaboran a partir de residuos orgánicos, como aceites usados de cocina y desechos agrícolas, ganaderos o forestales. Una alternativa que aprovecha materias primas que no compiten con la alimentación y puede reducir hasta un 90% las emisiones netas de CO₂ durante su ciclo de vida en comparación con los combustibles de origen fósil Descarbonización de sectores de difícil electrificación La primera fase del Valle Andaluz del Hidrógeno Verde contribuye a impulsar en Andalucía un ecosistema industrial en torno a las moléculas verdes. El proyecto contribuirá a descarbonizar sectores difíciles de electrificar, reforzar la competitividad de la industria y avanzar hacia una mayor autonomía energética Andalucía, energía y posición estratégica La combinación de recursos renovables, condiciones climáticas, tejido industrial, ubicación geográfica y grandes puertos ofrece a Andalucía condiciones favorables para producir moléculas verdes y contribuir a reforzar el papel de España en el nuevo mapa energético europeo Una transición que genera oportunidades Detrás de la transformación de la industria hay conocimiento, tecnología y trabajo en equipo. El desarrollo del proyecto movilizará una inversión de más de 1.000 millones de euros y contribuirá a generar nuevas oportunidades de empleo, inversión y colaboración empresarial en Andalucía, reforzando la competitividad de la industria española

Si las previsiones de Moeve se cumplen, Andalucía habrá transformado su capacidad industrial en menos de una década. “Podría consolidarse como uno de los principales hubs europeos de energías limpias y moléculas verdes”, afirma Molina. Algo que atraería también una mayor inversión internacional y un tejido empresarial “más innovador y especializado”.

Andalucía podría consolidarse como uno de los principales ‘hubs’ europeos de energías limpias y moléculas verdes María Molina, directora del Valle Andaluz del Hidrógeno Verde

En este escenario, la comunidad andaluza se posiciona como una plataforma energética para Europa. “Los primeros efectos comenzarán a notarse mucho antes, a medida que avancen las fases de construcción, se movilicen las inversiones y se incorporen las primeras empresas proveedoras a la cadena de valor”, explica la responsable del Valle Andaluz del Hidrógeno Verde. Más allá de la descarbonización, la iniciativa supone un punto de inflexión para reforzar la soberanía energética europea. “Y construir una economía más resiliente frente a futuras crisis geopolíticas y energéticas”, concluye.

World.title: He pagado una derrama de 5.000 euros para arreglar las filtraciones, pero la comunidad no inicia las obras. ¿Cómo reclamo?
World.content:
Pregunta. Tengo un inmueble en Tacoronte (Tenerife), donde residen mi hija y su familia. El edificio, dada su antigüedad y proximidad al mar, presenta serios problemas de revestimiento, filtraciones y riesgo de daños estructurales. Mi apartamento, en particular, padece filtraciones y humedades. La junta de propietarios aprobó una derrama destinada a financiar las obras y los honorarios profesionales. Hasta la fecha, he abonado una cantidad superior a 5.000 euros. Sin embargo, los trabajos aún no se han iniciado y ni el presidente ni la administración del edificio responden a mis correos o mensajes. ¿Qué pasos legales debo seguir para reclamar la ejecución de las obras o la solución a esta problemática? A. Gómez

Respuesta. Según el artículo 10.1.a) de la Ley 49/1960, de 21 de julio, de Propiedad Horizontal, la comunidad de propietarios está obligada a realizar las obras y actuaciones necesarias para el adecuado mantenimiento y conservación de los elementos comunes del edificio.

El hecho de que la presidencia y la administración de la finca no hayan llevado a cabo ninguna actuación, pese a haber aprobado y recaudado una derrama superior a 5.000 euros, supone un incumplimiento de las obligaciones inherentes a sus cargos dentro de la comunidad. En particular, la falta de gestión y ejecución de los acuerdos adoptados resulta contraria al artículo 20.1.c) de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, que impone al administrador la obligación de velar por la conservación de la finca.

Dado que sus comunicaciones informales no han obtenido respuesta, el siguiente paso sería enviar un burofax con acuse de recibo y certificación de contenido dirigido tanto al presidente como al administrador. En dicho escrito, puede concederles un plazo de diez días para que inicien las gestiones necesarias para ejecutar las obras o acrediten que ya han contratado los trabajos de reparación, indicando la fecha prevista de inicio, advirtiéndoles de que, en caso contrario, se ejercitarán las acciones legales oportunas.

Si transcurrido ese plazo continúan sin actuar, se podrá interponer una demanda por la vía civil solicitando al juez que requiera a la comunidad, representada por su presidente conforme al artículo 13.3 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, para que ejecute de forma inmediata las obras previamente aprobadas.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Porto Ercole, el pueblo de Italia donde la ‘dolce vita’ sigue mirando al mar
World.content:
Entre barcos de madera, terrazas frente al puerto y hoteles que forman parte de la historia del Mediterráneo y de la visión del fotógrafo Slim Aarons, en este enclave al sur de la Toscana la vida cotidiana sigue marcando el ritmo

Cuando llega la última hora de la tarde, la italiana Porto Ercole recupera su mejor versión. Los barcos regresan al puerto, las terrazas se llenan lentamente y la luz suaviza las fachadas de color ocre que trepan por la colina. Una Vespa atraviesa el paseo. Alguien recoge la ropa del balcón. Los camareros se mueven entre las mesas cuando llega la hora del aperitivo. En realidad nada parece extraordinario, y ahí está parte del encanto de este enclave en la costa del Argentario. La escena podría repetirse hoy o dentro de una década.

Este es uno de los lugares a los que la gente regresa. Las familias romanas que llevan generaciones pasando los veranos aquí. Los navegantes que conocen cada cala y quienes buscan un Mediterráneo que conserva su ritmo. Argentario no se parece demasiado a la Toscana que se suele imaginar. En vez de los campos infinitos de cipreses, aquí aparecen pinares que descienden hacia el mar y acantilados esculpidos por el viento.

Una callejuela en el casco antiguo de Porto Ercole. Atlantide Phototravel / GETTY IMAGES

Apenas a una hora y media en coche desde el aeropuerto de Roma (o en tren hasta Orbetello-Monte Argentario, a 10 kilómetros del pueblo), y a poco más de dos horas desde Pisa, los casi 3.000 vecinos de Porto Ercole han conseguido preservar algo cada vez más difícil de encontrar en el Mediterráneo: la sensación de estar en un lugar donde la vida cotidiana parece seguir marcando el ritmo.

Antes de que llegara Instagram, el fotógrafo estadounidense Slim Aarons (1916-2006) convirtió esta costa en uno de sus escenarios favoritos. Sus fotografías ayudaron a construir el imaginario de la dolce vita, retratando comidas interminables, barcos de madera, piscinas frente al mar y una elegancia que parecía surgir sin esfuerzo. Por delante de su cámara pasaron Gianni Agnelli, Lee Radziwill, los Getty o la familia Missoni… y muchas de aquellas escenas inmortalizadas siguen pareciendo posibles.

El encantador pueblo de Porto Ercole se encuentra en la costa del Argentario. Roberto Nencini ( GETTY IMAGES )

Las mañanas transcurren despacio en Porto Ercole; hay quienes comienzan el día con un expresso mirando al mar y los que prefieren perderse por las calles que rodean el puerto, donde se suceden pequeñas boutiques. Fue en una de esas tiendas donde empecé a entender mejor el pueblo. Había llegado la noche anterior y, después de descubrir que durante las noches aquí a veces corre un poco de fresco (aunque durante el verano son muy calientes, con temperaturas que suelen rondar los 30 grados de día y 25 grados de noche o más), entré en Ester Gi en busca de una capa ligera. Mientras me la probaba, Ornella, la encargada, empezó a hablar de Porto Ercole como solo hablan los italianos de los lugares que quieren. La Sirena para cenar pescado. O la Hosteria Alicina. O Il Gambero Rosso. Una recomendación llevaba a la siguiente y, antes de darme cuenta, ya no hablábamos de restaurantes, sino del pueblo. Ornella lo conoce bien, porque durante 14 años trabajó en la boutique del Hotel Il Pellicano y ha visto pasar generaciones de familias que repiten cada temporada. “Es como una pequeña joya”, dice al hablar del pueblo. “La gente vuelve porque aquí se sienten como en casa”.

Escuchándola, es fácil entender por qué, tarde o temprano, cualquier conversación sobre Porto Ercole acaba desembocando en el hotel Il Pellicano. “En realidad, toda su historia es una historia de amor”, explica. Y es difícil encontrar una mejor prueba de ello. Patricia Daszel, una socialité estadounidense, quedó fascinada por el piloto británico de guerra Michael Graham después de verlo fotografiado en un periódico como superviviente de un accidente aéreo. Años después se conocieron en Pelican Point, en California, se enamoraron y encontraron en unos terrenos de la familia Borghese, suspendidos sobre una cala de aguas cristalinas de Argentario, el lugar perfecto para construir una casa e invitar a sus amigos. Aquella residencia acabaría convirtiéndose en el hotel, que inauguraron en 1965.

Vista aérea del hotel Il Pellicano, en Porto Ercole. Pellicano Hotels

Ahora, 60 años después, Il Pellicano parece haber conservado una manera de entender el verano. Una buena parte de las fotografías más conocidas de Slim Aarons se tomaron aquí. El embarcadero, las plataformas junto al mar y las icónicas toallas de rayas amarillas y blancas siguen formando parte del paisaje. También la forma de vivirlo: un baño antes de comer, una sobremesa que se alarga y, al caer la tarde, el Bar Roberto, donde Federico Morosi lleva 18 años detrás de la barra.

La familia Sciò ha sido clave para conservar el carácter del alojamiento. Roberto Sciò llegó primero como huésped, se enamoró del lugar y lo hizo suyo en 1979. Desde entonces, el hotel ha mantenido esa combinación de elegancia relajada y discreción, hoy bajo la dirección de su hija Marie-Louise, y que también se percibe en La Posta Vecchia, la histórica propiedad familiar cerca de Roma.

Terraza junto al Mediterráneo de Il Pellicano. Pellicano Hotels

El espíritu de Il Pelicano también se percibe fuera del hotel. Ornella me insistió varias veces en que pasara por Medusa a la hora del aperitivo, un pequeño local abierto por Stefano y Alin, dos antiguos miembros del equipo que decidieron emprender su propio proyecto. Pedí una bruschetta de tomate y mozzarella mientras observaba la escena. Solo se escuchaba hablar italiano y sentí nostalgia de ese Mediterráneo de antes, con más veraneantes que turistas.

Cuando le pregunté a Ornella qué explicaba mejor Porto Ercole, no mencionó los hoteles ni los famosos. Habló de quienes crecieron veraneando aquí y siguen regresando cada año. Aunque esa fidelidad de la que hablaba no ha impedido que el pueblo empiece a escribir un nuevo capítulo. LA ROQQA es probablemente el mejor ejemplo. Inaugurado en 2023, hacía años que la apertura de un hotel no generaba tanta conversación en el pueblo. Mientras que Il Pellicano está más escondido sobre el acantilado, aquí el hotel forma parte de la vida cotidiana. Al cruzar la puerta, una puede mezclarse con las calles del centro o improvisar un aperitivo antes de regresar. Desde la entrada, donde suele descansar un pequeño Fiat descapotable que parece sacado de una fotografía de los años sesenta, LA ROQQA deja clara su personalidad. El interiorismo combina referencias retro, diseño contemporáneo y una paleta inspirada en los colores del puerto.

La mejor hora para subir a su rooftop Scirocco quizá no sea la cena, sino ese momento previo en el que el sol empieza a caer sobre Porto Ercole y el puerto cambia de color. La barra rinde homenaje a Caravaggio, con creaciones inspiradas en algunas de sus obras más célebres y reinterpretaciones del clásico Negroni. En la cocina también manda el producto local. Pescados del Tirreno, pasta fresca preparada a mano, verduras de temporada y vinos de la Toscana dan forma a la carta. Uno de los platos preferidos de la casa es su spaghetto otto pomodori, preparado con distintas variedades de tomate cultivadas en los alrededores de Porto Ercole.

La terraza Scirocco del hotel LA ROQQA, en Porto Ercole.

Explorando los alrededores

Quienes tienen algunos días más encuentran motivos de sobra para seguir explorando Argentario. A pocos minutos a pie desde Porto Ercole está la cala Le Viste. Hacia el norte, La Feniglia es una playa de arena bordeada por un pinar protegido perfecta para pasar la mañana, mientras que Spiaggia Lunga es más tranquila y salvaje.

Vista de la playa de La Feniglia. Andrea Pistolesi ( GETTY IMAGES )

La historia aparece donde menos se la espera. En Forte Filippo, fortaleza que los españoles levantaron en el siglo XVI para proteger la ruta marítima entre sus territorios italianos, y que sigue dominando la bahía a lo alto de las colinas. O en el último viaje de Caravaggio, que pasó aquí sus últimos días y murió en 1610 mientras intentaba regresar a Roma. A pocos kilómetros, Porto Santo Stefano es el punto de partida de los ferris hacia las islas de Giglio y Giannutri. Están integradas en el parque nacional del Archipiélago Toscano, el mayor parque marino protegido de Europa.

Porto Ercole conserva algo que resulta cada vez más difícil de encontrar, porque aquí las tardes siguen midiendo el tiempo en baños, aperitivos y conversaciones que se alargan sin mirar el reloj. Quizá por eso la dolce vita, más que una promesa, sigue pareciendo una forma de vivir.

World.title: Hundreds of thousands more to pay tax on savings, NOS says
World.content:
Hundreds of thousands more people in the Netherlands are set to pay tax on their savings and investments from 2028 under a revised plan for box 3, the tax on wealth, according to leaked details of the cabinet’s deliberations with opposition parties.

Box 3 covers savings, shares, crypto and second homes, and around 2.5 million people currently pay it, according to broadcaster NOS. At present the tax rate is 36% on an assumed return on those assets, with a tax-free allowance of €59,357 per person.

Under a new law on box 3 rules approved by MPs in February, people were to pay tax on unrealised returns on most assets every year, meaning they would pay tax on increased asset values regardless of whether they have sold the assets and made any money.

This plan is set to be dropped for shares, according to NOS, and people will only pay tax on gains from shares once they sell them. This was a demand by right-wing parties such as far-right JA21.

Initially, the new system was to allow a tax-free return of €1,800 per person a year. That has reportedly been cut to €1,000, helping offset the losses anticipated by moving to a realised gains system.

Businesses affected

People who run their own private limited company (bv) will also be affected. The amount they can borrow from their own company on favourable tax terms is set to fall from €500,000 to €100,000. The rules on borrowing from a company to buy a home will stay the same.

At the same time, tax on profits that owners pay out to themselves will be cut for 4 years. The aim is to encourage them to take money out of the company, which would bring in extra tax revenue in the short term.

The measures are expected to raise almost €500 million more than needed. The cabinet wants to use that to cut income tax, but has not yet said how.

Welfare cuts dropped

The leaked plans also confirm that planned cuts to social security are off the table, as left-wing Pro and pan-European party Volt said this week. Hans Spekman, chairman of the country’s largest trade union FNV, said on Monday evening that the unions would return to talks with the cabinet if the cuts were scrapped. Political sources told NOS that could happen as soon as next week.

JA21 said part of the funding for the box 3 changes was “unacceptable” because it hits small investors. Jan Struijs, parliamentary leader of pensioners’ party 50PLUS, said he wanted a “stress test” to show what the plans would mean for police officers, nurses and pensioners.

Finance minister Eelco Heinenis expected to set out the details in a letter to parliament ahead of this week’s budget debate. The minority cabinet needs opposition votes to get its budget through both houses of parliament.

World.title: Netherlands “blocked” Machado’s efforts to return to Venezuela
World.content:
The Dutch government has been accused of blocking the return of Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado after two flights to Curaçao and Aruba were cancelled on the same day.

Both flights were cancelled at short notice last Tuesday because of administrative “technicalities” that arose after Machado had booked to travel from her current home in Panama, according to a Spanish journalist who was embedded with her to document the trip.

The Nobel peace prize winner had hoped to slip into Venezuela via the Caribbean islands while the country’s interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, was in New York for the United Nations general assembly last week.

Officially the Netherlands supports Machado’s return so that free democratic elections can be held, something that has not happened since former president Nicolas Maduro was captured by US forces in January and replaced by Rodriguez, who was vice-president in Maduro’s regime.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said at his weekly press conference on Friday: “If Venezuela is serious about working towards a future where relations with the Netherlands and Europe are normalised, one of our conditions is that progress is made towards free and fair elections.

“Those elections are only possible if opposition leaders can participate in them.”

Trump oil deal

But behind the scenes, the Trump administration appears to be concerned that Machado’s return could destabilise the interim regime, which has struck a deal with Washington giving the US control of 65 billion barrels of crude oil reserves.

Leiden university professor Wouter Veenendaal, who specialises in relations between the nations in the Kingdom of the Netherlands, told Dutch News: “I can’t prove it, but it sounds to me like The Hague has been put under pressure by the Americans.

“Although the Americans formally take a positive view of Machado, her arrival is seen as potentially threatening the relative stability that they’ve been able to create with the interim president.”

Machado has made seven attempts to reach Venezuela by land, sea and air in recent months, including twice from Curaçao and once from Aruba, but every time her efforts have been thwarted by administrative or technical problems.

Last Tuesday a ferry trip from Panama City, where she is currently living, was cancelled hours before the boat was due to leave port after the operator claimed to have discovered a serious defect with the engine.

Paperwork problem

David Alandete, a journalist with the Spanish newspaper ABC who was invited to travel with Machado, said it was clear that the Dutch government, which controls the Caribbean islands’ foreign policy, “had a hand in preventing Machado from reaching Aruba, Curaçao or Bonaire”.

“This was not simply a paperwork problem. A European government was part of the chain of decisions that kept her from moving closer to Venezuela,” he wrote on social media site X.

Is María Corina Machado a prisoner in Panama? Why has the Nobel Peace Prize winner been prevented from returning to her own country seven times? I have the facts firsthand from Panama. I was with her team this weekend and witnessed the latest attempts—and the refusals. The full… pic.twitter.com/Jk4iBuop3m — David Alandete (@alandete) September 23, 2026

“Clearly there is something that is preventing Maria Corina Machado from returning,” Alandete said. “She has tried to enter and she’s been unable to do it.”

Jetten would neither confirm nor deny at his press conference whether the Netherlands was behind the decision to cancel Machado’s flights.

“It’s not in the interests of the co-operation we have with the [Venezuelan] opposition and the responsibility we feel for its members to say any more about it,” he said.

Caribbean journalists who asked Eric van der Burg, junior minister for kingdom relations, about the episode last week were redirected to the foreign affairs ministry in The Hague. “I can say extremely little about it,” he said, according to the Antilliaans Dagblad.

Jetten also hinted that he had been unable to persuade Rodriguez to guarantee Machado’s safe return to her country when he spoke to the interim president at the UN last week.

“It’s important that Machado and others are able to travel freely to Venezuela, and that’s why I brought it to the interim president’s attention.”

Veenendaal said the episode was typical of the way the Dutch govern Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao, which are semi-autonomous nations within the kingdom, and the “democratic deficit” in their administration.

Colonial history

The islands are represented by Van der Burg at the cabinet table in The Hague, but have no say in which issues are raised. Their parliaments have no powers to question cabinet ministers about foreign policy or defence.

“A lot of decisions are taken over their heads, which is a sensitive point given the colonial history,” Veenendaal said.

“In the past the Americans have exerted a lot of pressure on The Hague behind the scenes, for example to prevent the islands becoming independent, but also because they have air bases on the islands so that they can keep an eye on Venezuela.”

“I can see Jetten’s government thinking: ‘choose your battles’. Let the Americans get their way here so that the Americans give them an easier ride on other issues such as the International Criminal Court or Ukraine.”

World.title: Five arrested after luggage left unattended at railway stations
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Five people have been arrested after four railway stations had to be partly evacuated on Tuesday morning when luggage was left unattended.

Haarlem station and surrounding buildings were closed and cleared after two stray bags were reported at around 10.15am. Some trains were unable to stop at the station.

Luggage was also left standing in Rotterdam, Utrecht and Dordrecht. Police said there was no evidence that the incidents were linked, but they described the situation as “highly unusual”.

Three people were arrested at Haarlem station, while two others were detained at Utrecht Centraal after camera footage showed them acting suspiciously just before they dumped the bags.

In Rotterdam a pedestrian tunnel was evacuated while police checked two abandoned suitcases for possible explosives.

A woman in Rotterdam later came forward to say she had left the bags while she went into the city centre. She was not arrested.

Spokesman Jan Martijn Stout told NOS the incidents appeared to be unconnected, but the suspects were be questioned about why they had left the bags behind.

“Their role is being investigated because it was a significant disruption to public order,” he said.

World.title: Netherlands demands hundreds of billions in EU budget cuts
World.content:
The Dutch government has co-signed a letter to the EU presidency demanding the bloc’s next budget, which is set every seven years, be dramatically scaled back.

Prime minister Rob Jetten’s minority coalition is one of six so-called “frugal” governments, whose countries pay more into the EU budget than they get back.

The European Commission has proposed an almost €2 trillion budget for the 2028-2034 period, which governs spending on everything from agriculture to defence and funding for poorer regions.

Along with Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Austria, and Finland, the Netherlands is now pressing for a cut of several hundred billion euros from the proposals.

The letter, which has not been made public but has been seen by major news outlets, states: “Our six countries alone finance almost 40% of all Member States’ contributions. While net contributors as a whole are in the minority, they shoulder around three-quarters of the total financing burden.”

An almost €2 trillion budget would represent a 60% nominal increase in the size of the current budget, which, they argue, is “simply not realistic.”

Divisions

There are 17 other countries, including Spain and Italy, who are insisting on protections for impoverished regions and struggling sectors like agriculture, and want the overall budget raised above €2 trillion.

The Commission has also suggested creating new EU-wide taxes, including a levy on large companies and a tobacco excise duty, to raise capital and ease the burden on countries like the Netherlands. In June, the Cypriot presidency proposed a 2% cut to the Commission’s plan, which the six considered far too small.

Negotiators want to get a deal done by the end of the year, before elections in France, Italy, Spain and Poland complicate the talks. All 27 member states must agree to the budget.

But according to the Financial Times, a diplomat from one of the six countries said there would be no deal this year unless the budget was cut by hundreds of billions of euros.

Ireland, which currently holds the rotating EU presidency, is due to present a new compromise text in the coming days, ahead of a summit of EU leaders on October 15 and 16. European Council president António Costa will meet Jetten in the Netherlands on October 9 to discuss the budget.

Jetten’s shift

The letter marks a U-turn for Jetten, whose D66 party went into the 2025 election calling for a European budget twice its current size, financed by new EU-level taxes. The same manifesto proposed €750 to €800 billion a year in extra European investment, paid for with joint borrowing.

In office with his minority coalition, Jetten has taken a different line. At an informal EU summit in Cyprus in April, he rejected the €2 trillion proposal, telling reporters the Dutch contribution would “explode” under the plan, according to De Telegraaf. In June he told NOS the Commission’s proposal was “simply not good enough”.

A big part of the reason is money – at the moment, the Netherlands gets a discount on its EU bill. Brussels wants to end that discount, which would cost the Dutch around €2 billion more a year. In total, the plans would add up to €5.4 billion a year to what the Netherlands pays the EU, according to the Court of Audit, the government’s spending watchdog.

World.title: Five things every first-time buyer in the Netherlands must know
World.content:
Buying your first home is one of the biggest financial decisions most people make in their lives. And as an international in the Netherlands, it’s likely that the process, language and unwritten rules are all different from what you might expect.

Cherene Kruger, founder of Homes for Expats, has spent years helping international buyers through their first Dutch house purchase, and her starting point is always the same: don’t assume the process works the way it does back home.

“The biggest problem is you don’t know what you don’t know,” she says. “You’re not shopping for property on your home turf, which already makes things stressful.” In the Netherlands, that unfamiliar cast list includes two makelaars (estate agents), a bank, a mortgage adviser and a notary: roles that may not exist, or might work quite differently, elsewhere.

The estate agent isn’t on your side

The most important thing to understand, says Cherene, is who actually represents whom. “The selling makelaar represents the seller. If you appoint a buying makelaar, they are the one representing your interests and fighting in your corner.”

“I once had a client who kept saying out loud how much she was prepared to pay for a house, right in front of the selling agent,” she says.

It’s a distinction that doesn’t occur to a lot of first-time buyers, and one whose consequences Cherene has experienced herself. She once bought a new-build property that didn’t automatically come with plastered and painted walls, a paved driveway or a levelled garden with grass, because no one had properly explained what was and wasn’t included beforehand.

Don’t get caught up in overbidding

While overbidding is often a fact of life in the Dutch market, knowing how much to offer can be one of the hardest things for international buyers to navigate. The asking price doesn’t reflect market value, and simply offering more isn’t always the right decision.

Cherene also sees more buyers turning to AI for answers. “AI can be a useful research tool, but it cannot replace someone being on the ground, seeing the property, understanding what’s happening in that particular market and having actual lived experience.”

Cherene’s own approach is deliberately pragmatic: research the area, weigh market value against what a property is actually worth, and look at comparable sales, understand the market value and then decide what the property is worth to you as a buyer. “My job is to help you make the right decision and the right investment,” she says. “You’re buying a house, not a hamburger, so it’s incredibly important we get this right!” She would rather see a client lose a property than win one at a cost that leaves them in negative equity for years to come.

Get financing sorted before you fall for a house

Every offer Cherene puts together includes two standard conditions: a financing clause and a technical inspection. Both protect the buyer. If financing falls through without a financing condition, the buyer could face a penalty of 10% of the purchase price. A technical inspection condition offers protection if serious defects are uncovered.

For instance, the inspection can unearth problems like hidden mould or rotten beams that aren’t obvious during a viewing. “If there’s a major issue that is going to cost my clients a lot of money, I would rather walk away from a bad relationship than marry just for the sake of getting married.” Depending on how the technical inspection condition has been agreed, serious defects may give the buyer the opportunity to renegotiate or withdraw from the purchase.

For buyers relocating for work, getting that financial picture in order early is arguably the single most useful thing they can do. Once a client signs with Homes for Expats, Cherene advises them to register with a mortgage adviser or their bank and have their documents submitted before the serious house hunting begins. That way, they know what’s actually affordable and are in a position to move when they find the right home.

Homes for Expats sets out the buying process in more detail, but the underlying message is consistent: have the financing conversation before the house hunting starts, not after you’ve found the one.

What you see isn’t necessarily what you get

One of Cherene’s most vivid cases involved an apartment marketed as a two-bedroom, which her clients fell in love with. When she started digging into the property’s deed of division, however, the numbers didn’t add up: the apartment was around 10 square metres smaller on the deed than advertised, and that second “bedroom” up a flight of stairs was in fact a storage room.

The room wasn’t listed on the deed of division as residential space, the deed of division had never been amended to change its designated use, and the previous owner had never obtained permission to convert the storage space into liveable accommodation, either from the gemeente (local council) or from the building’s VvE (owners’ association).

Cherene is clear on the lesson: “Triple-check everything. A property’s paperwork, the deed of division, VvE permissions and permit history can tell a very different story from the one a listing suggests. And if something isn’t documented, there’s probably a reason for that.”

Dutch rules may not be what you’d expect

A recurring misconception is that owning property automatically means being free to rent it out for extra income, as it might elsewhere. In the Netherlands, that’s not necessarily the case. Your mortgage conditions, municipal rules, VvE rules and Dutch tenancy law can all affect whether and how a property may be rented.

“Most people have been taught you can generate wealth this way,” she says, “but it’s different in the Netherlands.” It’s a reminder that runs through all of Cherene’s advice: assume nothing carries over from home, however similar it looks on the surface.

Getting the keys

Cherene admits to a soft spot for first-time buyers specifically: “If I do my job well, I set the bar for every real estate transaction they’ll ever make. You’ll always remember the first home you buy. I get to be part of people’s joy, and for me that is my “why’”.

“I love helping people, and this fits so perfectly into that part of me. If I do my job right, I haven’t just helped them buy a house. I’ve been part of them buying their very first home, something they will never forget.”

For many of her clients, most of them a long way from where they grew up, the moment they get the keys is about more than the property itself. It’s the point at which the Netherlands really feels like home.

For anyone starting to think about buying, Cherene’s advice is simple: get your financial ducks in a row, and book a free chat with Homes for Expats before you start house hunting.

World.title: Amsterdam university bans laptops and mobiles from lecture hall
World.content:

Students who have enrolled for a sociology course at the University of Amsterdam this year have been told to leave electronic devices at the door and go back to taking notes by hand.

The UvA has banned laptops, mobile phones and tablets from lectures and classes in interdisciplinary social science, on the grounds that they interefere with students’ concentration.

Senior lecturer Cyrilien Evertsen told NOS that “60% to 80% of students are doing things on digital devices during classes other than listening”, such as shopping or chatting on social media. “They’re not mentally present in the class,” she said.

Paul Kirschner, emeritus professor of educational psychology at Utrecht University, backed the stance, arguing that switching off devices and taking notes by hand makes students engage directly with the lecture material.

“Switch off all electronic devices because it’s a weapon of mass distraction,” he said.

“If you’re checking your email, you’re not following the class,” he said. “You might think that’s not so bad, but research has shown that people to your left and right get distracted and do significantly worse as a result.”

He added that handwriting forced students to select and summarise what information they take down because it is a slower process than typing.

“So you’re digesting the information, and learning is digesting,” he said.

World.title: Amsterdam man arrested over links to ShinyHunters hacking group
World.content:
A 24-year-old man from Amsterdam has been arrested on suspicion of involvement with the hacking group ShinyHunters, which has been behind a number of large-scale attacks on Dutch businesses in the past year.

Police said on social media that he was arrested this month and will appear in court in Rotterdam on Wednesday.

Sources told broadcaster NOS that the suspect is Pepijn van der S., who was sentenced to four years in prison in 2023 for extortion, money laundering and hacking. He was released this year.

Van der S. reportedly has a background in legitimate cybersecurity, having worked for Amsterdam-based security firm Hadrian. He also carried out ethical hacking research with the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure. At the same time, he was leaking data stolen from clients and other companies, the court found in 2023.

ShinyHunters was responsible for an attack on Dutch telecoms provider Odido earlier this year, in which millions of customers had their personal data stolen. After the company refused to pay a ransom, the group posted much of the data on the dark web.

The hackers were also behind an attack on Canvas, an online learning platform used by students, after which its parent company paid a ransom to prevent further disruption.

Last week, ShinyHunters also claimed to have accessed the details of thousands of employees at the FBI, the US federal law enforcement agency. The FBI said an investigation was underway.

World.title: The IamExpat Fair is back in Eindhoven: what’s new this year?
World.content:
The IamExpat Fair returns to Eindhoven on Saturday October 3 for its second outing in the city, with a bigger careers section, two international centres and a new kids area.

The fair, which takes place in the Klokgebouw in Strijp-S, provides advice and services of all kinds for the international community, including special offers only available for attendees. You can register for free online.

“We are bringing back the large career section, expanding the number of expat centres at the fair, and growing the Family & Kids section,” says event manager Claire Leunissen.

Workshops and presentations

The fair will also feature over 20 free workshops to help expats with job hunting, finding housing, immigration and settling advice, as well as tips on local leisure and health services, and more. The workshops have limited capacity and are filling up fast, so make sure to book seats as soon as possible — you can sign up here.

Careers and partners

The careers section includes Brainport and recruitment agency Undutchables, and offers additional advice and services for the partners of people who have moved to the region for work.

“The international community of Eindhoven can’t be underestimated,” says Claire. “Because of this small but mighty community, we are bringing the Fair back to Eindhoven to support internationals and their families looking to to settle into Dutch life as well, through career opportunities, community groups, fitness schools, Dutch classes, and more.”

Families and newcomers

New this year is a kids area, supervised by childcare provider Korein, where families can play while parents work their way round the stands.

Two international centres will be on hand for questions about registration and residency: Holland Expat Center South, based in Eindhoven, and Expat Centre Maastricht Region. Orion Immigration Law returns with a stand double the size of last year’s.

Language schools include Language Institute Regina Coeli in Vught, Una Paloma Blanca, Bart de Pau and Taalkracht, while the health and leisure exhibitors range from bike subscription service Swapfiets to Happy Bodies and Shakti Nutrition.

Every stage covered

Workshops and presentations by experts run for most of the day, covering renting, buying a house and securing a mortgage, tax, careers and schooling.

“The fair is an incredible one-stop shop for every part of life in the Netherlands,” says Claire. “International students or young professionals may initially come to the Fair looking for Dutch language classes or career opportunities, but later in life, they come to the Fair for different needs, such as preparing for retirement, buying their first home, or choosing the right daycare for their kids.”

“We are excited to bring the IamExpat Fair back to the Klokgebouw, a historic building that embodies the history of technology, innovation and immigration of Eindhoven,” says Claire.

The IamExpat Fair Eindhoven takes place in the Klokgebouw, Strijp-S on Saturday October 3 from 10am to 5pm. Entrance is free with online registration.

World.title: EU court rejects Poland’s request to suspend implementation of Mercosur trade deal
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The Court of Justice of the European Union has rejected a request from Poland to suspend the implementation of the EU’s recently launched free trade agreement with the Mercosur bloc of South American countries. The CJEU found that the Polish government had failed to prove its claims that the trade deal would cause serious harm to European farmers, consumers or the environment. #ECJ: Order in Case C-460/26 R Poland v Council: should the implementation of the Council’s decision authorising the provisional application of the EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement be suspended pending the Court’s ruling?#CJEU #Mercosur pic.twitter.com/ocb4I4PsE8 — EU Court of Justice (@EUCourtPress) September 29, 2026 Poland has long been critical of the agreement, in particular over the potential negative impact that imports of agricultural products from Mercosur, which includes Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, could have on Polish farmers, who have repeatedly protested against the deal. In January, Poland failed in a bid to block the agreement at the European Council, where 21 of the EU’s 27 member states voted in favour of the deal. Although the agreement has not yet received final ratification – still requiring approval from the European Parliament and national parliaments – it nevertheless went into provisional force on 1 May. Shortly afterwards, Poland submitted a complaint to the CJEU, calling for implementation of the agreement to be suspended. It argued, first of all, that the process through which the deal had been provisionally implemented violated the EU’s treaties. Second, it claimed that liberalising trade in agricultural products without imposing the same production standards in both the EU and Mercosur created a risk of harm to human and animal health, the environment, the income of farmers, and the functioning of the market in the EU. Poland has filed a complaint to the European Court of Justice against the EU's free-trade deal with the South American Mercosur bloc that recently went into provisional force. It wants the agreement to be suspended until the court issues a ruling https://t.co/wE7DIbDazU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 However, on Tuesday, the CJEU announced that it had dismissed the application to suspend the agreement, finding that “Poland has not provided any concrete evidence to establish the likelihood and imminence of serious and irreparable damage”. The court pointed out that agricultural products from Mercosur could already be imported to the EU before the free-trade deal, and that they were and continue to be subject to food safety and health regulations similar to those for products manufactured in the EU. It also noted that the new trade deal includes tools allowing the EU to bar products that do not meet standards, including emergency measures in the case of a serious threat to human, animal or plant life. Finally, the CJEU said that Poland’s “general and abstract claims” regarding potential harm to farmers and markets did not include “any evidence capable of establishing, with a sufficient degree of probability, that the implementation [of the agreement]…will cause disruption”. In response to the court’s decision, the Polish government’s spokesman, Adam Szłapka, immediately blamed the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) administration, which was in power in Poland from 2015 to 2023. Szłapka said that the details of the Mercosur deal had been agreed during that period and that PiS had “failed to secure Polish interests in any way”. He argued that it was the current government which secured the addition of last-minute safeguards intended to protect farmers. The spokesman also noted that Polish agricultural exports to the Mercosur bloc have actually increased under the new agreement while imports from there have fallen, showing that “Polish farmers are profiting from this”. Rząd i Premier Tusk najpierw mówili, że umowa UE-Mercosur będzie „bezpieczna dla polskich rolników”. Potem nie potrafili zbudować koalicji blokującej w Radzie Europejskiej – choć polityka europejska jest domeną rządu. Politycy KO, PSL i Lewicy nie potrafili nikogo przekonać.… https://t.co/EqOJr4sneP — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) September 29, 2026 However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the foreign policy office of President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the CJEU’s decision showed the impotence of the current pro-EU government. “The government and Prime Minister Tusk first said that the EU-Mercosur agreement would be ‘safe for Polish farmers’. Then they failed to build a blocking coalition in the European Council,” wrote Przydacz. “In the end, under pressure from public opinion in Poland, they filed a complaint with the ECJ. [It was] so weak that they lost the request for interim relief,” he added. “Ineffective policy and ineffective government.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland recovers looted painting that once hung in SS officers’ club in occupied Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish painting looted by Nazi Germany during World War Two, and which once hung in an SS officers’ club, has been returned by its owner, who donated it to the National Museum in Warsaw. “History is coming home,” said culture minister Marta Cienkowska, celebrating the return of Alfred Wierusz-Kowalski’s Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow, which she described as “one of the most significant wartime losses in Polish painting”. Her ministry is responsible for seeking the return of tens of thousands of artworks and other cultural items that were looted during the war and remain missing. Kolejny sukces restytucyjny! Odzyskaliśmy jedną z cenniejszych i najbardziej znanych strat wojennych malarstwa polskiego. Obraz „Zima – Odwrót Napoleona spod Moskwy” Alfreda Wierusza-Kowalskiego trafił dziś do zbiorów Muzeum Narodowego w Warszawie. To efekt naszej współpracy z… pic.twitter.com/Y0wDIBgIGG — Ministerstwo Kultury i Dziedzictwa Narodowego (@kultura_gov_pl) September 28, 2026 Wierusz-Kowalski, who was active in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, was a renowned realist painter whose work often featured animals alongside people. His Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow had, by the 1930s, become part of the collection of Andrzej Rotwand, a wealthy banker and industrialist. In June 1939, it was featured in an exhibition organised by the Society for the Encouragement of Fine Arts in Warsaw, which occupied the building that is now the famous Zachęta National Gallery of Art. However, the exhibition was brought to an abrupt end when Nazi Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. The works on display, along with other items from the gallery, were seized by the occupiers, with many used to decorate the offices and apartments of German officials. Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow was displayed in a club for high-ranking SS and police officers located in Warsaw’s Blanka Palace. The same building also housed Warsaw’s German-installed commissioner, Helmut Otto, and mayor, Ludwig Leist. No information has been released as to the fate of the painting in the immediate aftermath of the war. However, it eventually came into the possession of Ewa Tsonis, who has now handed it back. Speaking at a ceremony in the National Museum in Warsaw, Tsonis said that her late father, Michał Stefan Koryzna, had purchased the painting in the 1960s from Desa, a major gallery and auction house, in the city of Kraków. “I grew up with this painting. It was greatly appreciated and loved in our family,” she said. However, after recently conducting research into the painting’s history, she became aware of its provenance and notified the culture ministry. Experts from the National Museum in Warsaw confirmed the identity of the painting, which remains in good condition and in its original frame. Tsonis then donated the work to the museum. “Restitution is not possible without the cooperation of many people and institutions – both on the side of the state and on the part of the owners of the works,” said Cienkowska, who thanked Tsonis for her “incredibly responsible and civic-minded attitude”. “Such attitudes are still rare but, because we constantly talk about restitution – we search for lost works and strive to recover them – we are increasingly approached by people who own lost objects and feel a sense of responsibility for cultural heritage.” Cienkowska noted that the culture ministry has so far secured the return of over 920 works, with around 200 more restitution cases currently underway in 18 countries. Germany has agreed to return to Poland a collection of 73 medieval documents that were looted during WWII. The culture minister has hailed it as "the most important and valuable return of stolen cultural heritage in modern Polish history" https://t.co/GxHQ8A0jyr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 1, 2025 However, that is still just a small fraction of the over 60,000 missing items listed in the ministry’s database of missing works, which includes seven further paintings by Wierusz-Kowalski. Two other works from Rotwand’s collection – Italian Woman by Anna Bilińska and Mother with Children by Kazimierz Alchimowicz – were also hung in the SS officers’ club during the war and today remain missing. Poland has in recent years stepped up efforts to secure the return of historical and cultural items looted during the German and Soviet occupations. In 2022, it appealed to UNESCO for help in securing the return of cultural items that remain missing after being looted by Nazi Germany. It also launched a campaign seeking the return of thousands of items that ended up in Russia after the war. World.title: Poland changes rules of engagement for firing on foreign aircraft amid growing Russia threat
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
